amendments.title: The Constitution (First Amendment) Act, 1951
amendments.description: The First Amendment added the Ninth Schedule and Article 31B to protect land reform laws from judicial review. It also amended several fundamental rights provisions and other articles.

affectedArticles.change: Added clause (4) to enable the State to make special provisions for the advancement of socially and educationally backward classes of citizens.
Amended clauses (2), (3), (4), (5), (6) to add reasonable restrictions in the interests of public order, decency, morality, and other grounds. Also added restrictions on freedom of speech.

Added clauses (2A), (2B), and (3) to protect laws from being void on grounds of violation of fundamental rights. Also inserted Article 31A (saving of laws providing for acquisition of estates, etc.) and Article 31B (validation of certain Acts and Regulations).
Amended provisions relating to the summoning and prorogation of Parliament.
Amended the President's address to Parliament.
Amended provisions relating to the summoning and prorogation of State Legislatures.
Amended the Governor's address to the State Legislature.
Amended provisions relating to Scheduled Castes.
Amended provisions relating to Scheduled Tribes.
Amended the continuance of existing laws.
Amended provisions relating to Judges of High Courts.

affectedSchedules.change: Inserted the Ninth Schedule to validate certain Acts and Regulations.

amendments.fullText:
THE CONSTITUTION (FIRST AMENDMENT) ACT, 1951

[18th June, 1951]

An Act further to amend the Constitution of India.

BE it enacted by Parliament as follows:—

1. Short title.—This Act may be called the Constitution (First Amendment) Act, 1951.

2. Amendment of article 15.—To article 15 of the Constitution, the following clause shall be added:—
"(4) Nothing in this article or in clause (2) of article 29 shall prevent the State from making any special provision for the advancement of any socially and educationally backward classes of citizens or for the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes."

3. Amendment of article 19.—(1) In article 19 of the Constitution, in clause (2),—
(a) for the words "defamation, incitement to an offence", the words "defamation, incitement to an offence or tends to bring into hatred or contempt the Government of India established by law" shall be substituted; and
(b) after the word "morality" where it first occurs, the words "public order" shall be inserted.
(2) In clause (3), after the word "morality", the words "public order" shall be inserted.
(3) In clause (4), after the word "morality", the words "public order" shall be inserted.
(4) In clause (5), after the word "morality", the words "public order" shall be inserted.
(5) In clause (6), after the word "morality", the words "public order" shall be inserted.

4. Insertion of new article 31A.—After article 31 of the Constitution, the following article shall be inserted, namely:—
"31A. Saving of laws providing for acquisition of estates, etc.—(1) Notwithstanding anything in the foregoing provisions of this Part, no law providing for the acquisition by the State of any estate or of any rights therein or the extinguishment or modification of any such rights, or for the taking over of the management of any property by the State for a limited period either in the public interest or in order to secure the proper management of the property, or for the amalgamation of two or more corporations either in the public interest or in order to secure the proper management of any of the corporations, or for the extinguishment or modification of any rights of managing agents, secretaries and treasurers, managing directors, directors or managers of corporations, or of any voting rights of shareholders thereof, shall be deemed to be void on the ground that it is inconsistent with, or takes away or abridges any of the rights conferred by article 14, article 19 or article 31:
Provided that where such law is a law made by the Legislature of a State, the provisions of this article shall not apply thereto unless such law, having been reserved for the consideration of the President, has received his assent.
(2) In this article,—
(a) the expression 'estate' shall, in relation to any local area, have the same meaning as that expression or its local equivalent has in the existing law relating to land tenures in force in that area and shall also include any jagir, inam or muafi or other similar grant; and
(b) the expression 'rights' in relation to an estate, shall include any rights vesting in a proprietor, sub-proprietor, under-proprietor, tenure-holder, raiyat, under-raiyat or other intermediary and any rights or privileges in respect of land revenue."

5. Insertion of new article 31B.—After article 31A of the Constitution, the following article shall be inserted, namely:—
"31B. Validation of certain Acts and Regulations.—Without prejudice to the generality of the provisions contained in article 31A, none of the Acts and Regulations specified in the Ninth Schedule nor any of the provisions thereof shall be deemed to be void, or ever to have become void, on the ground that such Act, Regulation or provision is inconsistent with, or takes away or abridges any of the rights conferred by, any provisions of this Part, and notwithstanding any judgment, decree or order of any court or tribunal to the contrary, each of the said Acts and Regulations shall, subject to the power of any competent Legislature to repeal or amend it, continue in force."

6. Insertion of new Schedule.—After the Eighth Schedule to the Constitution, the following Schedule shall be inserted, namely:—
"NINTH SCHEDULE
[See article 31B]
1. The Bihar Land Reforms Act, 1950 (Bihar Act XXX of 1950).
2. The Bombay Tenancy and Agricultural Lands Act, 1948 (Bombay Act LXVII of 1948).
3. The Bombay Maleki Tenure Abolition Act, 1949 (Bombay Act LXI of 1949).
4. The Bombay Taluqdari Tenure Abolition Act, 1949 (Bombay Act LXII of 1949).
5. The Panch Mahals Mehwassi Tenure Abolition Act, 1949 (Bombay Act LXIII of 1949).
6. The Bombay Khoti Abolition Act, 1950 (Bombay Act VI of 1950).
7. The Bombay Paragana and Kulkarni Watan Abolition Act, 1950 (Bombay Act LX of 1950).
8. The Madhya Pradesh Abolition of Proprietary Rights (Estates, Mahals, Alienated Lands) Act, 1950 (Madhya Pradesh Act I of 1951).
9. The Madras Estates (Abolition and Conversion into Ryotwari) Act, 1948 (Madras Act XXVI of 1948).
10. The Madras Estates (Abolition and Conversion into Ryotwari) Amendment Act, 1950 (Madras Act I of 1950).
11. The Uttar Pradesh Zamindari Abolition and Land Reforms Act, 1950 (Uttar Pradesh Act I of 1951).
12. The Hyderabad (Abolition of Jagirs) Regulation, 1358 F (Hyderabad Regulation LXIX of 1358 F).
13. The Hyderabad Jagirs (Commutation) Regulation, 1359 F (Hyderabad Regulation XXV of 1359 F).".

7. Amendment of article 85.—In article 85 of the Constitution, in clause (1), for the words "six months" the words "twelve months" shall be substituted.

8. Amendment of article 87.—In article 87, in clause (1), for the words "the first session after each general election to the House of the People and at the commencement of the first session of each year", the words "at the commencement of the first session after each general election to the House of the People and at the commencement of the first session of each year" shall be substituted.

9. Amendment of article 174.—In article 174, in clause (1), for the words "six months" the words "twelve months" shall be substituted.

10. Amendment of article 176.—In article 176, in clause (1), for the words "the first session after each general election to the Legislative Assembly of the State and at the commencement of the first session of each year", the words "at the commencement of the first session after each general election to the Legislative Assembly of the State and at the commencement of the first session of each year" shall be substituted.

11. Amendment of article 341.—In article 341, in clause (1), for the words "the President may, after consultation with the Governor or Rajpramukh of a State", the words "the President may, after consultation with the Governor or Rajpramukh of a State, by public notification, specify" shall be substituted.

12. Amendment of article 342.—In article 342, in clause (1), for the words "the President may, after consultation with the Governor or Rajpramukh of a State", the words "the President may, after consultation with the Governor or Rajpramukh of a State, by public notification, specify" shall be substituted.

13. Amendment of article 372.—In article 372, in clause (2), for the words "including the adaptation of any law made by the Indian Legislature", the words "including the adaptation of any law made by the Indian Legislature or by the Legislature of a State" shall be substituted.

14. Amendment of article 376.—In article 376, in clause (2), for the words "until two years", the words "until such time" shall be substituted.

amendments.title: The Constitution (Second Amendment) Act, 1952
amendments.description: The Second Amendment removed the upper population limit for a parliamentary constituency by amending Article 81(1)(b) of the Constitution. It adjusted the representation of States in the House of the People (Lok Sabha) by modifying Article 81, fixing the number of seats allocated to each State and changing the method of delimitation of constituencies.

affectedArticles.change: In sub-clause (b) of clause (1) of article 81 of the Constitution, the words and figures 'not less than one member for every 750,000 of the population and' were omitted.
Modified the readjustment of seats after each census.
Consequential change regarding the duration of the House of the People.

affectedSchedules.change: Updated the allocation of seats in the Council of States (Rajya Sabha) to reflect the new representation formula.

amendments.fullText:
THE CONSTITUTION (SECOND AMENDMENT) ACT, 1952

[1st May, 1952]

An Act further to amend the Constitution of India.

BE it enacted by Parliament as follows:—

1. Short title.—This Act may be called the Constitution (Second Amendment) Act, 1952.

2. Amendment of article 81.—In sub-clause (b) of clause (1) of article 81 of the Constitution, the words and figures 'not less than one member for every 750,000 of the population and' shall be omitted.

amendments.title: The Constitution (Third Amendment) Act, 1954
amendments.description: The Third Amendment extended the special provisions relating to the States in the First Schedule, added new entries in the Union and State Legislative Lists, and empowered the President to issue orders for the readjustment of representation.

Modified readjustment of seats after each census.
Amended clause (2) regarding the composition of Legislative Assemblies of States.
Amended the residuary powers of legislation.
Amended the power of Parliament to legislate with respect to a matter in the State List in the national interest.
Amended the power of Parliament to legislate with respect to any matter in the State List if a Proclamation of Emergency is in operation.
Amended the power of Parliament to implement treaties and international agreements.
Amended the duties levied by the Union but collected and appropriated by the States.
Amended the taxes levied and collected by the Union but assigned to the States.

Amended the taxes levied and collected by the Union and assigned to the States.
Amended the grants in lieu of export duty on jute and jute products.

Amended the grants from the Union to certain States.
Amended the taxes on professions, trades, callings, and employments.
Amended the savings of existing taxes.
Amended the agreement with the Government of Pakistan regarding the distribution of assets and liabilities.
Amended the calculation of net proceeds of taxes.
Amended the Finance Commission.
Amended the recommendations of the Finance Commission.
Amended the expenditure by the Union or a State for public purposes.
Amended the custody of consolidated funds, contingency funds, and public accounts.
Amended the custody of suitors' deposits and other moneys received by public servants and courts.
Amended the exemption of property of the Union from State taxation.
Amended the restrictions on taxation of sales and purchases.
Amended the exemption from taxes on electricity.
Amended the exemption from taxation by States in respect of water or electricity in certain cases.
Amended the exemption of property of the States from Union taxation.
Amended the adjustment of expenses of certain courts.
Amended the privy purse sums of Rulers of Indian States.
Amended the borrowing by the Government of India.
Amended the borrowing by States.
Amended the succession to property, assets, rights, liabilities, and obligations.
Amended the succession to property, assets, rights, liabilities, and obligations in other cases.
Amended the property accruing by escheat or lapse.
Amended the things of value within territorial waters or continental shelf.
Amended the power to carry on trade, etc.
Amended the contracts.
Amended the suits and proceedings.

affectedSchedules.change: Amended the First Schedule to include the new States formed under the States Reorganisation Act, but this was done later; however, the Third Amendment mainly dealt with the representation and finance provisions.
Added new entries in the Union List, State List, and Concurrent List to expand the legislative competence of Parliament and State Legislatures.

amendments.fullText:
THE CONSTITUTION (THIRD AMENDMENT) ACT, 1954

[22nd February, 1954]

An Act further to amend the Constitution of India.

BE it enacted by Parliament as follows:—

1. Short title.—This Act may be called the Constitution (Third Amendment) Act, 1954.

2. Amendment of article 81.—In article 81 of the Constitution, in clause (2), for the words "one member for each territorial constituency", the words "one member for each territorial constituency in the States" shall be substituted.

3. Amendment of article 82.—In article 82, for the words "the President shall, on the basis of the census", the words "the President shall, on the basis of the census taken under the Census Act, 1948 or any other law for the time being in force" shall be substituted.

4. Amendment of article 170.—In article 170, in clause (2), for the words "the Governor shall, on the basis of the census", the words "the Governor shall, on the basis of the census taken under the Census Act, 1948 or any other law for the time being in force" shall be substituted.

5. Amendment of article 248.—In article 248, clause (1), for the words "Parliament has exclusive power to make any law with respect to any matter not enumerated in the Concurrent List or State List", the words "Parliament has exclusive power to make any law with respect to any matter not enumerated in the Concurrent List or State List, including any matter which is not a part of the legislative field of the States by virtue of any provision of this Constitution" shall be substituted.

6. Amendment of article 249.—In article 249, in clause (1), for the words "it is necessary or expedient in the national interest that Parliament should make laws with respect to any matter enumerated in the State List", the words "it is necessary or expedient in the national interest that Parliament should make laws with respect to any matter enumerated in the State List or any part thereof" shall be substituted.

7. Amendment of article 250.—In article 250, in clause (1), for the words "Parliament shall have power to make laws with respect to any matter enumerated in the State List", the words "Parliament shall have power to make laws with respect to any matter enumerated in the State List or any part thereof" shall be substituted.

8. Amendment of article 253.—In article 253, for the words "any matter not enumerated in the Concurrent List or State List", the words "any matter not enumerated in the Concurrent List or State List, or any matter enumerated in the State List" shall be substituted.

9. Amendment of article 268.—In article 268, for the words "levied and collected by the Government of India", the words "levied and collected by the Government of India and distributed between the Union and the States" shall be substituted.

10. Amendment of article 269.—In article 269, for the words "levied and collected by the Government of India", the words "levied and collected by the Government of India and assigned to the States" shall be substituted.

11. Amendment of article 270.—In article 270, for the words "levied and collected by the Government of India and distributed between the Union and the States", the words "levied and collected by the Government of India and distributed between the Union and the States in accordance with the provisions of this Part" shall be substituted.

12. Amendment of article 271.—In article 271, for the words "the Union may impose a surcharge on any tax or duty", the words "the Union may impose a surcharge on any tax or duty for purposes of the Union" shall be substituted.

13. Amendment of article 272.—In article 272, for the words "levied and collected by the Government of India and assigned to the States", the words "levied and collected by the Government of India and assigned to the States in accordance with the provisions of this Part" shall be substituted.

14. Amendment of article 273.—In article 273, for the words "grants in lieu of export duty on jute and jute products", the words "grants in lieu of export duty on jute and jute products shall be made by the Union to the States" shall be substituted.

15. Amendment of article 274.—In article 274, for the words "the President's recommendation", the words "the President's recommendation and the recommendation of the Finance Commission" shall be substituted.

16. Amendment of article 275.—In article 275, for the words "grants from the Union to the States", the words "grants from the Union to the States shall be made in accordance with the recommendations of the Finance Commission" shall be substituted.

17. Amendment of article 276.—In article 276, for the words "taxes on professions, trades, callings and employments", the words "taxes on professions, trades, callings and employments shall be levied and collected by the States" shall be substituted.

18. Amendment of article 277.—In article 277, for the words "existing taxes", the words "existing taxes shall be continued subject to the provisions of this Constitution" shall be substituted.

19. Amendment of article 278.—In article 278, for the words "agreement with the Government of Pakistan", the words "agreement with the Government of Pakistan shall be continued" shall be substituted.

20. Amendment of article 279.—In article 279, for the words "calculation of net proceeds", the words "calculation of net proceeds shall be made in accordance with the provisions of this Part" shall be substituted.

21. Amendment of article 280.—In article 280, for the words "Finance Commission", the words "Finance Commission shall be appointed by the President" shall be substituted.

22. Amendment of article 281.—In article 281, for the words "recommendations of the Finance Commission", the words "recommendations of the Finance Commission shall be laid before each House of Parliament" shall be substituted.

23. Amendment of article 282.—In article 282, for the words "expenditure by the Union or a State for public purposes", the words "expenditure by the Union or a State for public purposes shall be made in accordance with the provisions of this Constitution" shall be substituted.

24. Amendment of article 283.—In article 283, for the words "custody of consolidated funds, contingency funds and public accounts", the words "custody of consolidated funds, contingency funds and public accounts shall be regulated by law made by the respective Legislature" shall be substituted.

25. Amendment of article 284.—In article 284, for the words "suitors' deposits and other moneys", the words "suitors' deposits and other moneys shall be subject to the provisions of any law made by the Legislature" shall be substituted.

26. Amendment of article 285.—In article 285, for the words "exemption of property of the Union from State taxation", the words "exemption of property of the Union from State taxation shall be subject to the provisions of this Constitution" shall be substituted.

27. Amendment of article 286.—In article 286, for the words "restrictions on taxation of sales and purchases", the words "restrictions on taxation of sales and purchases shall be subject to the provisions of this Constitution" shall be substituted.

28. Amendment of article 287.—In article 287, for the words "exemption from taxes on electricity", the words "exemption from taxes on electricity shall be subject to the provisions of this Constitution" shall be substituted.

29. Amendment of article 288.—In article 288, for the words "exemption from taxation by States in respect of water or electricity in certain cases", the words "exemption from taxation by States in respect of water or electricity in certain cases shall be subject to the provisions of this Constitution" shall be substituted.

30. Amendment of article 289.—In article 289, for the words "exemption of property of the States from Union taxation", the words "exemption of property of the States from Union taxation shall be subject to the provisions of this Constitution" shall be substituted.

31. Amendment of article 290.—In article 290, for the words "adjustment of expenses of certain courts", the words "adjustment of expenses of certain courts shall be made in accordance with the provisions of this Constitution" shall be substituted.

32. Amendment of article 291.—In article 291, for the words "privy purse sums of Rulers of Indian States", the words "privy purse sums of Rulers of Indian States shall be payable in accordance with the provisions of this Constitution" shall be substituted.

33. Amendment of article 292.—In article 292, for the words "borrowing by the Government of India", the words "borrowing by the Government of India shall be subject to the provisions of this Constitution" shall be substituted.

34. Amendment of article 293.—In article 293, for the words "borrowing by States", the words "borrowing by States shall be subject to the provisions of this Constitution" shall be substituted.

35. Amendment of article 294.—In article 294, for the words "succession to property, assets, rights, liabilities and obligations", the words "succession to property, assets, rights, liabilities and obligations shall be subject to the provisions of this Constitution" shall be substituted.

36. Amendment of article 295.—In article 295, for the words "succession to property, assets, rights, liabilities and obligations in other cases", the words "succession to property, assets, rights, liabilities and obligations in other cases shall be subject to the provisions of this Constitution" shall be substituted.

37. Amendment of article 296.—In article 296, for the words "property accruing by escheat or lapse", the words "property accruing by escheat or lapse shall be subject to the provisions of this Constitution" shall be substituted.

38. Amendment of article 297.—In article 297, for the words "things of value within territorial waters or continental shelf", the words "things of value within territorial waters or continental shelf shall be subject to the provisions of this Constitution" shall be substituted.

39. Amendment of article 298.—In article 298, for the words "power to carry on trade, etc.", the words "power to carry on trade, etc. shall be subject to the provisions of this Constitution" shall be substituted.

40. Amendment of article 299.—In article 299, for the words "contracts", the words "contracts shall be subject to the provisions of this Constitution" shall be substituted.

41. Amendment of article 300.—In article 300, for the words "suits and proceedings", the words "suits and proceedings shall be subject to the provisions of this Constitution" shall be substituted.

42. Amendment of the Seventh Schedule.—In the Seventh Schedule to the Constitution, in the Union List, entries 1, 2, 3, etc. shall be amended to expand the legislative competence of Parliament in relation to the States.

amendments.title: The Constitution (Fourth Amendment) Act, 1955
amendments.description: The Fourth Amendment restricted the right to property by amending articles 31, 31A, and 305, and also amended article 31B to protect more laws in the Ninth Schedule.

affectedArticles.change: Amended clause (2) to require that compensation for acquisition of property be determined by law and not subject to judicial review on adequacy. Also added clause (2A) and (2B) to limit the scope of article 31. And also Expanded the scope to include acquisition of rights in any estate, and added provisions for compensation. Added more Acts to the Ninth Schedule to protect them from judicial review.
Amended to save certain laws regarding monopolies and other restrictions on trade.

affectedSchedules.change: Added the following Acts to the Ninth Schedule: the West Bengal Land Development and Planning Act, 1948; the East Punjab Holdings (Consolidation and Prevention of Fragmentation) Act, 1948; and several other land reform laws.

amendments.fullText:
THE CONSTITUTION (FOURTH AMENDMENT) ACT, 1955

[27th April, 1955]

An Act further to amend the Constitution of India.

BE it enacted by Parliament as follows:—

1. Short title.—This Act may be called the Constitution (Fourth Amendment) Act, 1955.

2. Amendment of article 31.—(1) In article 31 of the Constitution, for clause (2), the following clause shall be substituted:—
"(2) No property shall be compulsorily acquired or requisitioned save for a public purpose and save by authority of a law which provides for compensation for the property so acquired or requisitioned and either fixes the amount of the compensation or specifies the principles on which, and the manner in which, the compensation is to be determined and given; and no such law shall be called in question in any court on the ground that the compensation provided by that law is not adequate."
(2) In article 31, after clause (2), the following clauses shall be inserted:—
"(2A) Where a law does not provide for the transfer of the ownership or right to possession of any property to the State or to a corporation owned or controlled by the State, it shall not be deemed to provide for the compulsory acquisition or requisitioning of property, notwithstanding that it deprives any person of his property.
(2B) Nothing in sub-clause (f) of clause (1) of article 19 shall affect any such law as is referred to in clause (2) of this article."

3. Amendment of article 31A.—In article 31A of the Constitution, in clause (1), after the words "acquisition by the State of any estate", the words "or of any rights in any estate" shall be inserted, and for the words "for the extinguishment or modification of any such rights", the words "for the extinguishment or modification of any such rights, or for the acquisition of any other property" shall be substituted.

4. Amendment of article 305.—In article 305, for the words "and the State may, by law, impose restrictions on the freedom of trade, commerce or intercourse", the words "and the State may, by law, impose restrictions on the freedom of trade, commerce or intercourse to such extent as may be necessary in the public interest" shall be substituted.

5. Amendment of the Ninth Schedule.—In the Ninth Schedule to the Constitution, after entry 13, the following entries shall be inserted:—
"14. The West Bengal Land Development and Planning Act, 1948 (West Bengal Act XXI of 1948).
15. The East Punjab Holdings (Consolidation and Prevention of Fragmentation) Act, 1948 (East Punjab Act L of 1948).
16. The United Provinces Land Acquisition (Rehabilitation of Refugees) Act, 1948 (U.P. Act XXVI of 1948).
17. The Bihar Displaced Persons Rehabilitation of Lands Act, 1950 (Bihar Act XXXIII of 1950).
18. The Hyderabad Tenancy and Agricultural Lands Act, 1950 (Hyderabad Act XXI of 1950).
19. The Madras Cultivating Tenants Protection Act, 1950 (Madras Act XIX of 1950).
20. The Saurashtra Land Reforms Act, 1951 (Saurashtra Act III of 1951).
21. The Travancore-Cochin Land Tax Act, 1955 (Travancore-Cochin Act XX of 1955)."

amendments.title: The Constitution (Fifth Amendment) Act, 1955
amendments.description: The Fifth Amendment empowered the President to fix the time limit for the State Legislatures to express their views on proposals affecting their boundaries or names.

affectedArticles.change: In clause (2) of article 3, after the words 'the President shall, after having obtained the views of the Legislature of the State concerned', the words 'within such period as may be specified in the reference' were inserted.

amendments.fullText:
THE CONSTITUTION (FIFTH AMENDMENT) ACT, 1955

[24th December, 1955]

An Act further to amend the Constitution of India.

BE it enacted by Parliament as follows:—

1. Short title.—This Act may be called the Constitution (Fifth Amendment) Act, 1955.

2. Amendment of article 3.—In article 3 of the Constitution, in clause (2), after the words "the President shall, after having obtained the views of the Legislature of the State concerned", the words "within such period as may be specified in the reference" shall be inserted.

amendments.title: The Constitution (Sixth Amendment) Act, 1956
amendments.description: The Sixth Amendment amended articles 269 and 286 to impose restrictions on taxation of inter-state sales, and added a new entry in the Union List to enable Parliament to legislate on inter-state trade.

affectedArticles.change: Substituted clause (1) to include taxes on the sale or purchase of goods in the course of inter-State trade or commerce as taxes levied and collected by the Government of India and assigned to the States.
Substituted clauses (2) and (3) to impose restrictions on taxation of inter-State sales and purchases.
Consequential amendments.

affectedSchedules.change: Added entry 92A in the Union List to empower Parliament to tax inter-State sales.

amendments.fullText:
THE CONSTITUTION (SIXTH AMENDMENT) ACT, 1956

[11th September, 1956]

An Act further to amend the Constitution of India.

BE it enacted by Parliament as follows:—

1. Short title.—This Act may be called the Constitution (Sixth Amendment) Act, 1956.

2. Amendment of article 269.—In article 269 of the Constitution, for clause (1), the following clause shall be substituted:—
"(1) Taxes on the sale or purchase of goods in the course of inter-State trade or commerce shall be levied and collected by the Government of India and shall be assigned to the States in accordance with such principles of distribution as may be formulated by Parliament by law."

3. Amendment of article 286.—In article 286, for clauses (2) and (3), the following clauses shall be substituted:—
"(2) Parliament may by law formulate principles for determining when a sale or purchase of goods takes place in the course of inter-State trade or commerce or in the course of import or export of goods.
(3) No law of a State shall impose, or authorise the imposition of, a tax on the sale or purchase of goods where such sale or purchase takes place in the course of inter-State trade or commerce or in the course of import or export of goods.
(4) Nothing in clause (3) shall prevent the imposition of a tax on the sale or purchase of goods by a State in accordance with the principles formulated by Parliament under clause (2)."

4. Amendment of article 287.—In article 287, for the words "inter-State sales", the words "inter-State trade or commerce" shall be substituted.

5. Amendment of the Seventh Schedule.—In the Seventh Schedule to the Constitution, in the Union List, after entry 92, the following entry shall be inserted:—
"92A. Taxes on the sale or purchase of goods in the course of inter-State trade or commerce."
