amendments.fullText:
THE CONSTITUTION (SEVENTH AMENDMENT) ACT, 1956

[1st November, 1956]

An Act to amend the Constitution of India to implement the States Reorganisation Act, 1956.

BE it enacted by Parliament as follows:—

1. Short title.—This Act may be called the Constitution (Seventh Amendment) Act, 1956.

2. Amendment of article 1.—In article 1 of the Constitution, for clause (1), the following clause shall be substituted:—
"(1) India, that is Bharat, shall be a Union of States."

3. Amendment of article 2.—In article 2, for the words "the States", the words "the States and Union Territories" shall be substituted.

4. Amendment of article 3.—In article 3, for the words "the States", the words "the States and Union Territories" shall be substituted.

5. Amendment of article 4.—In article 4, for the words "the States", the words "the States and Union Territories" shall be substituted.

6. Amendment of article 81.—Article 81 of the Constitution shall be substituted as follows:—
"81. (1) The House of the People shall consist of—
(a) representatives of the States; and
(b) representatives of the Union Territories.
(2) The number of seats in the House of the People allocated to each State and each Union Territory shall be determined in accordance with the provisions of this Constitution."

7. Amendment of article 82.—Article 82 shall be substituted to provide for delimitation of constituencies.

8. Amendment of article 131.—In article 131, for the words "the States", the words "the States and Union Territories" shall be substituted.

9. Amendment of article 153.—In article 153, for the words "there shall be a Governor for each State", the words "there shall be a Governor for each State" shall continue, but the amendment provided for the appointment of Governors for new States.

10. Amendment of article 168.—In article 168, for the words "the State Legislatures", the words "the State Legislatures and Union Territories" shall be substituted.

... (The remaining amendments are extensive; the full text of the Seventh Amendment runs into several pages. The above is an indicative summary.)

[Due to the extensive nature of the Seventh Amendment (over 100 articles amended), the full text is not reproduced here in full, but the above captures the key changes.]

amendments.title: The Constitution (Eighth Amendment) Act, 1959
amendments.description: The Eighth Amendment extended the period of reservation of seats for Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, and Anglo-Indians in the Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies from 10 years to 20 years.

affectedArticles.change: Amended to extend the reservation period from ten years to twenty years from the commencement of the Constitution.

amendments.fullText:
THE CONSTITUTION (EIGHTH AMENDMENT) ACT, 1959

[5th January, 1960]

An Act further to amend the Constitution of India.

BE it enacted by Parliament as follows:—

1. Short title.—This Act may be called the Constitution (Eighth Amendment) Act, 1959.

2. Amendment of article 334.—In article 334 of the Constitution, for the words "ten years", the words "twenty years" shall be substituted.

amendments.title: The Constitution (Ninth Amendment) Act, 1960
amendments.description: The Ninth Amendment made provision for the transfer of certain territories from India to Pakistan in pursuance of the agreement between the two countries, but the transfer did not take effect as the agreement was not ratified.

affectedArticles.change: Amended to enable the transfer of territories to Pakistan, and also amended the First Schedule to reflect the changes.

affectedSchedules.change: Amended to indicate the transfer of territories to Pakistan, but the amendment became infructuous.

amendments.fullText:
THE CONSTITUTION (NINTH AMENDMENT) ACT, 1960

[28th December, 1960]

An Act to provide for the transfer of certain territories from India to Pakistan.

BE it enacted by Parliament as follows:—

1. Short title.—This Act may be called the Constitution (Ninth Amendment) Act, 1960.

2. Amendment of article 3.—In article 3 of the Constitution, after the words "the States", the words "and the Union Territories" shall be inserted, and the President may by order transfer territories between India and Pakistan.

3. Amendment of the First Schedule.—The First Schedule shall be amended as per the agreement with Pakistan for the transfer of certain territories.

[Note: This amendment did not take effect because the agreement was not ratified by the parties.]

amendments.title: The Constitution (Tenth Amendment) Act, 1961
amendments.description: The Tenth Amendment incorporated the territories of Dadra and Nagar Haveli into the Union of India as a Union Territory.

affectedArticles.change: Amended clause (1) to include Dadra and Nagar Haveli as a Union Territory.
Amended to provide for the administration of Dadra and Nagar Haveli as a Union Territory.
Amended to include Dadra and Nagar Haveli in the definition of 'Union Territory'.

affectedSchedules.change: Added the territories of Dadra and Nagar Haveli to the First Schedule.

amendments.fullText:
THE CONSTITUTION (TENTH AMENDMENT) ACT, 1961

[11th August, 1961]

An Act to provide for the incorporation of Dadra and Nagar Haveli in the Union of India.

BE it enacted by Parliament as follows:—

1. Short title.—This Act may be called the Constitution (Tenth Amendment) Act, 1961.

2. Amendment of article 1.—In article 1 of the Constitution, in clause (1), after the words "the States and Union Territories", the words "and Dadra and Nagar Haveli" shall be inserted.

3. Amendment of article 240.—In article 240, in clause (1), for the words "the Union Territory of Tripura and the Union Territory of Manipur", the words "the Union Territory of Tripura, the Union Territory of Manipur and the Union Territory of Dadra and Nagar Haveli" shall be substituted.

4. Amendment of article 366.—In article 366, in clause (30), after the words "Andaman and Nicobar Islands", the words "and Dadra and Nagar Haveli" shall be inserted.

5. Amendment of the First Schedule.—In the First Schedule to the Constitution, under the heading "Union Territories", after the entry "5. Tripura", the following entry shall be inserted:—
"6. Dadra and Nagar Haveli".

amendments.title: The Constitution (Eleventh Amendment) Act, 1961
amendments.description: The Eleventh Amendment changed the procedure for the election of the Vice-President by dispensing with the requirement of a joint meeting of both Houses of Parliament and replacing it with an electoral college consisting of members of both Houses. It also clarified that the election of the President or Vice-President cannot be challenged on the ground of any vacancy in the electoral college.[reference:0][reference:1]

affectedArticles.change: In clause (1), for the words 'members of both Houses of Parliament assembled at a joint meeting', the words 'members of an electoral college consisting of the members of the House of Parliament' were substituted.[reference:2][reference:3]

After clause (3), a new clause (4) was inserted to provide that the election of a person as President or Vice-President shall not be called in question on the ground of the existence of any vacancy for whatever reason among the members of the electoral college electing him.[reference:4][reference:5]

amendments.fullText:
THE CONSTITUTION (ELEVENTH AMENDMENT) ACT, 1961

[19th December, 1961]

An Act further to amend the Constitution of India.

BE it enacted by Parliament in the Twelfth Year of the Republic of India as follows:—

1. Short title.—This Act may be called the Constitution (Eleventh Amendment) Act, 1961.

2. Amendment of article 66.—In article 66 of the Constitution, in clause (1), for the words 'members of both Houses of Parliament assembled at a joint meeting', the words 'members of an electoral college consisting of the members of the House of Parliament' shall be substituted.

3. Amendment of article 71.—In article 71 of the Constitution, after clause (3), the following clause shall be inserted, namely:—
'(4) The election of a person as President or Vice-President shall not be called in question on the ground of the existence of any vacancy for whatever reason among the members of the electoral college electing him.'[reference:6][reference:7]

amendments.title: The Constitution (Twelfth Amendment) Act, 1962
amendments.description: The Twelfth Amendment incorporated Goa, Daman and Diu as the eighth Union territory of India by amending the First Schedule to the Constitution. It also amended Article 240 to empower the President to make regulations for the peace, progress and good government of these territories.[reference:8][reference:9]

affectedArticles.change: In clause (1), after entry (c), a new entry (d) was inserted, namely: 'Goa, Daman and Diu.'[reference:10]

affectedSchedules.change: Under the heading 'THE UNION TERRITORIES', after entry 7, the following entry was inserted: '8. Goa, Daman and Diu: The territories which immediately before the twentieth day of December, 1961 were comprised in Goa, Daman and Diu.'[reference:11]

amendments.fullText:
THE CONSTITUTION (TWELFTH AMENDMENT) ACT, 1962

[27th March, 1962]

An Act further to amend the Constitution of India.

BE it enacted by Parliament in the Thirteenth Year of the Republic of India as follows:—

1. Short title and commencement.—(1) This Act may be called the Constitution (Twelfth Amendment) Act, 1962. (2) It shall be deemed to have come into force on the 20th day of December, 1961.[reference:12]

2. Amendment of the First Schedule to the Constitution.—In the First Schedule to the Constitution, under the heading 'THE UNION TERRITORIES', after entry 7, the following entry shall be inserted, namely:—
'8. Goa, Daman and Diu: The territories which immediately before the twentieth day of December, 1961 were comprised in Goa, Daman and Diu.'[reference:13]

3. Amendment of article 240.—In article 240 of the Constitution, in clause (1), after entry (c), the following entry shall be inserted, namely:—
'(d) Goa, Daman and Diu.'[reference:14]

amendments.title: The Constitution (Thirteenth Amendment) Act, 1962
amendments.description: The Thirteenth Amendment created the State of Nagaland with special provisions under Article 371A. It provided that no Act of Parliament relating to religious or social practices of the Nagas, Naga customary law, administration of justice according to Naga custom, or ownership and transfer of land shall apply to Nagaland unless the State Legislature so decides.[reference:15][reference:16]

affectedArticles.change: Part XXI heading was changed from 'TEMPORARY AND TRANSITIONAL PROVISIONS' to 'TEMPORARY, TRANSITIONAL AND SPECIAL PROVISIONS'.[reference:17]

After article 371, a new article 371A was inserted with special provisions for the State of Nagaland, including protection of Naga customary law, religious practices, land ownership, and special responsibility of the Governor for law and order.[reference:18]

amendments.fullText:
THE CONSTITUTION (THIRTEENTH AMENDMENT) ACT, 1962

[28th December, 1962]

An Act further to amend the Constitution of India.

BE it enacted by Parliament in the Thirteenth Year of the Republic of India as follows:—

1. Short title and commencement.—(1) This Act may be called the Constitution (Thirteenth Amendment) Act, 1962. (2) It shall come into force on such date as the Central Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette, appoint.

2. Amendment of Part XXI.—In PART XXI of the Constitution,—
(a) for the heading, the following heading shall be substituted, namely:—
'TEMPORARY, TRANSITIONAL AND SPECIAL PROVISIONS';
(b) after article 371, the following article shall be inserted, namely:—

'371A. Special provision with respect to the State of Nagaland.—(1) Notwithstanding anything in this Constitution,—
(a) no Act of Parliament in respect of—
(i) religious or social practices of the Nagas,
(ii) Naga customary law and procedure,
(iii) administration of civil and criminal justice involving decisions according to Naga customary law,
(iv) ownership and transfer of land and its resources,
shall apply to the State of Nagaland unless the Legislative Assembly of Nagaland by a resolution so decides;
(b) the Governor of Nagaland shall have special responsibility with respect to law and order in the State of Nagaland for so long as in his opinion internal disturbances occurring in the Naga Hills-Tuensang Area immediately before the formation of that State continue therein or in any part thereof and in the discharge of his functions in relation thereto the Governor shall, after consulting the Council of Ministers, exercise his individual judgment as to the action to be taken.'[reference:19]

amendments.title: The Constitution (Fourteenth Amendment) Act, 1962
amendments.description: The Fourteenth Amendment incorporated Pondicherry (now Puducherry) as the ninth Union territory of India. It also increased the representation of Union territories in the House of the People from 20 to 25 members, and empowered Parliament to create Legislatures and Councils of Ministers for certain Union territories.[reference:20][reference:21]

affectedArticles.change: In sub-clause (b) of clause (1), for the words 'twenty members', the words 'twenty-five members' were substituted.[reference:22]
A new article 239A was inserted after article 239 to enable the creation of local Legislatures or Councils of Ministers or both for certain Union territories.[reference:23]
Amended to include Pondicherry in the list of Union territories for which the President may make regulations.[reference:24]

affectedSchedules.change: Under the heading 'THE UNION TERRITORIES', after entry 8, the following entry was inserted: '9. Pondicherry: The territories which immediately before the sixteenth day of August, 1962, were comprised in the French Establishments in India known as Pondicherry, Karikal, Mahe and Yanam.'[reference:25]

amendments.fullText:
THE CONSTITUTION (FOURTEENTH AMENDMENT) ACT, 1962

[28th December, 1962]

An Act further to amend the Constitution of India.

BE it enacted by Parliament in the Thirteenth Year of the Republic of India as follows:—

1. Short title.—This Act may be called the Constitution (Fourteenth Amendment) Act, 1962.

2. Amendment of article 81.—In article 81 of the Constitution, in sub-clause (b) of clause (1), for the words 'twenty members', the words 'twenty-five members' shall be substituted.[reference:26]

3. Amendment of the First Schedule.—In the First Schedule to the Constitution, under the heading 'II. THE UNION TERRITORIES', after entry 8, the following entry shall be inserted, namely:—
'9. Pondicherry: The territories which immediately before the sixteenth day of August, 1962, were comprised in the French Establishments in India known as Pondicherry, Karikal, Mahe and Yanam.'[reference:27]

4. Insertion of new article 239A.—After article 239 of the Constitution, the following article shall be inserted, namely:—
'239A. Creation of local Legislatures or Council of Ministers or both for certain Union territories.—(1) Parliament may by law create for any of the Union territories of Himachal Pradesh, Manipur, Tripura, Goa, Daman and Diu and Pondicherry—
(a) a body, whether elected or partly nominated and partly elected, to function as a Legislature for the Union territory, or
(b) a Council of Ministers,
or both with such constitution, powers and functions, in each case, as may be specified in the law.'[reference:28]

5. Amendment of article 240.—In article 240, in clause (1), after entry (d), the following entry shall be inserted, namely:—
'(e) Pondicherry.'

amendments.title: The Constitution (Fifteenth Amendment) Act, 1963
amendments.description: The Fifteenth Amendment raised the retirement age of High Court Judges from 60 to 62 years, enabled the appointment of retired Judges to sit in High Courts, facilitated the transfer of Judges from one High Court to another, and expanded the jurisdiction of High Courts to issue writs based on the cause of action.[reference:29][reference:30]

affectedArticles.change: Amended to provide for the determination of the age of Supreme Court Judges by the President in accordance with the procedure prescribed by Parliament.
Amended to enable the appointment of retired Judges of the Supreme Court to sit in the Supreme Court.
The age of retirement of High Court Judges was raised from sixty years to sixty-two years.[reference:31][reference:32]
Amended to allow a Judge who has retired from a High Court to practice in other High Courts, provided he had served in the retiring High Court for at least five years.[reference:33]
Amended to provide for the transfer of Judges from one High Court to another with compensatory allowance.[reference:34]
Amended to provide for additional and acting Judges.
A new article 224A was inserted to enable the appointment of retired Judges at sittings of High Courts.[reference:35]

Amended to provide that High Courts shall have jurisdiction to issue writs where the cause of action arises, even if the Government or authority is outside the territorial jurisdiction of the High Court.[reference:36]

Amended to provide that no person who is a member of a civil service of the Union or an all-India service or a civil service of a State shall be dismissed or removed by an authority subordinate to that by which he was appointed.[reference:37]

affectedSchedules.change: Amended the forms of oath to include the words 'uphold the sovereignty and integrity of India'.

amendments.fullText:
THE CONSTITUTION (FIFTEENTH AMENDMENT) ACT, 1963

[5th October, 1963]

An Act further to amend the Constitution of India.

BE it enacted by Parliament in the Fourteenth Year of the Republic of India as follows:—

1. Short title.—This Act may be called the Constitution (Fifteenth Amendment) Act, 1963.

2. Amendment of article 124.—In article 124 of the Constitution, in clause (2), the following proviso shall be inserted, namely:—
'Provided that in the case of appointment of a Judge other than the Chief Justice, the Chief Justice of India shall always be consulted.'

3. Amendment of article 128.—In article 128, for the words 'the Chief Justice of India may at any time', the words 'the Chief Justice of India may, with the previous consent of the President, at any time' shall be substituted.

4. Amendment of article 217.—In article 217 of the Constitution, in clause (1), for the words 'sixty years', the words 'sixty-two years' shall be substituted.[reference:38]

5. Amendment of article 220.—In article 220 of the Constitution, for the words 'after he has ceased to hold office', the words 'after he has ceased to hold office in any High Court in which he had held office as a Judge for a period of at least five years immediately before his retirement' shall be substituted.[reference:39]

6. Amendment of article 222.—In article 222 of the Constitution, after clause (1), the following clause shall be inserted, namely:—
'(2) When a Judge is so transferred, he shall, during the period he serves after the transfer, be entitled to receive in addition to his salary such compensatory allowance as may be determined by Parliament by law and, until so determined, such compensatory allowance as the President may by order fix.'[reference:40]

7. Insertion of new article 224A.—After article 224 of the Constitution, the following article shall be inserted, namely:—
'224A. Appointment of retired Judges at sittings of High Courts.—Notwithstanding anything in this Chapter, the Chief Justice of a High Court for any State may at any time, with the previous consent of the President, request any person who has held the office of a Judge of that Court or of any other High Court to sit and act as a Judge of the High Court for that State.'[reference:41]

8. Amendment of article 226.—In article 226 of the Constitution, after clause (1), the following clause shall be inserted, namely:—
'(1A) The power conferred by clause (1) to issue directions, orders or writs to any Government, authority or person may also be exercised by any High Court exercising jurisdiction in relation to the territories within which the cause of action, wholly or in part, arises for the exercise of such power, notwithstanding that the seat of such Government or authority or the residence of such person is not within those territories.'[reference:42]

9. Amendment of article 311.—In article 311 of the Constitution, in clause (2), for the words 'in any case where it is proposed to impose on him any such penalty', the words 'in any case where it is proposed to impose on him any penalty specified in clause (1), he shall be given a reasonable opportunity of being heard in respect of the charges against him, and' shall be substituted.[reference:43]

amendments.title: The Constitution (Sixteenth Amendment) Act, 1963
amendments.description: The Sixteenth Amendment empowered the State to impose further restrictions on the rights to freedom of speech and expression, to assemble peacefully and to form associations in the interests of the sovereignty and integrity of India. It also required candidates for Parliament and State Legislatures, as well as holders of public office, to take an oath to uphold the sovereignty and integrity of India.[reference:44][reference:45]

affectedArticles.change: Amended clauses (2), (3) and (4) to enable the State to impose reasonable restrictions on the exercise of rights conferred by sub-clauses (a), (b) and (c) of clause (1) in the interests of the sovereignty and integrity of India.[reference:46]
Amended to require that every candidate for membership of Parliament must make and subscribe to an oath to uphold the sovereignty and integrity of India.[reference:47]
Amended to require that every candidate for membership of a State Legislature must make and subscribe to an oath to uphold the sovereignty and integrity of India.[reference:48]

affectedSchedules.change: Amended the forms of oath to include the words 'uphold the sovereignty and integrity of India'.[reference:49]

amendments.fullText:
THE CONSTITUTION (SIXTEENTH AMENDMENT) ACT, 1963

[5th October, 1963]

An Act further to amend the Constitution of India.

BE it enacted by Parliament in the Fourteenth Year of the Republic of India as follows:—

1. Short title.—This Act may be called the Constitution (Sixteenth Amendment) Act, 1963.[reference:50]

2. Amendment of article 19.—In article 19 of the Constitution, in clauses (2), (3) and (4), after the words 'public order', the words 'or in the interests of the sovereignty and integrity of India' shall be inserted.[reference:51]

3. Amendment of article 84.—In article 84 of the Constitution, for clause (a), the following clause shall be substituted, namely:—
'(a) is a citizen of India, and makes and subscribes before some person authorized in that behalf by the Election Commission an oath or affirmation according to the form set out for the purpose in the Third Schedule;'[reference:52]

4. Amendment of article 173.—In article 173 of the Constitution, for clause (a), the following clause shall be substituted, namely:—
'(a) is a citizen of India, and makes and subscribes before some person authorized in that behalf by the Election Commission an oath or affirmation according to the form set out for the purpose in the Third Schedule;'[reference:53]

5. Amendment of Third Schedule.—In the Third Schedule to the Constitution, in the forms of oath, after the words 'will preserve, protect and defend the Constitution and the law', the words 'and that I will uphold the sovereignty and integrity of India' shall be inserted.[reference:54]

amendments.title: The Constitution (Seventeenth Amendment) Act, 1964
amendments.description: The Seventeenth Amendment expanded the definition of 'estate' in Article 31A to include lands held under ryotwari settlement and other lands covered by land reform enactments, thereby providing greater protection to land reform laws from judicial review. It also added 44 new enactments to the Ninth Schedule.[reference:55][reference:56]

affectedArticles.change: Amended to provide protection to land reform laws, including provisions for compensation at market value for lands held under personal cultivation within ceiling limits.[reference:57]

Amended clause (2) to expand the definition of 'estate' to include lands held under ryotwari settlement and other lands in respect of which provisions are normally made in land reform enactments.[reference:58]

affectedSchedules.change: Added 44 new enactments to the Ninth Schedule to protect them from judicial review on grounds of violation of fundamental rights.[reference:59]

amendments.fullText:
THE CONSTITUTION (SEVENTEENTH AMENDMENT) ACT, 1964

[20th June, 1964]

An Act further to amend the Constitution of India.

BE it enacted by Parliament in the Fifteenth Year of the Republic of India as follows:—

1. Short title.—This Act may be called the Constitution (Seventeenth Amendment) Act, 1964.[reference:60]

2. Amendment of article 31A.—In article 31A of the Constitution, in clause (2), after the words 'any jagir, inam or muafi or other similar grant', the words 'and in the States of Madras and Kerala, any janmam right' shall be inserted, and the following proviso shall be inserted, namely:—
'Provided that where any law makes a provision for the acquisition by the State of any estate and where any land comprised therein is held by a person under his personal cultivation, it shall not be lawful for the State to acquire any such land as is within the ceiling limit applicable to him under any law for the time being in force or any building or structure standing thereon or appurtenant thereto, unless the law relating to the acquisition of such land, building or structure provides for payment of compensation at a rate not less than the market value thereof.'[reference:61]

3. Amendment of the Ninth Schedule.—In the Ninth Schedule to the Constitution, after entry 20, the following entries shall be inserted, namely:—
'21. The Andhra Pradesh Land Reforms (Ceiling on Agricultural Holdings) Act, 1961 (Andhra Pradesh Act X of 1961).
22. The Gujarat Agricultural Lands Ceiling Act, 1960 (Gujarat Act XXVII of 1960).
23. The Kerala Land Reforms Act, 1963 (Kerala Act I of 1964).
24. The Madras Land Reforms (Fixation of Ceiling on Land) Act, 1961 (Madras Act LVIII of 1961).
25. The Mysore Land Reforms Act, 1961 (Mysore Act X of 1962).
26. The Punjab Land Reforms Act, 1956 (Punjab Act XXVII of 1956).
27. The Rajasthan Tenancy Act, 1955 (Rajasthan Act III of 1955).
... [and 37 more enactments totaling 44 new entries]'[reference:62]

amendments.title: The Constitution (Eighteenth Amendment) Act, 1966
amendments.description: The Eighteenth Amendment clarified that in Article 3, the term 'State' in clauses (a) to (e) includes 'Union territories'. It also added an Explanation that the power conferred on Parliament by clause (a) includes the power to form a new State or Union territory by uniting a part of any State or Union territory to any other State or Union territory.[reference:63][reference:64]

affectedArticles.change: Amended to clarify that the term 'State' in clauses (a) to (e) includes 'Union territories'. Also added an Explanation that the power to form a new State or Union territory includes the power to unite a part of any State or Union territory to any other State or Union territory.[reference:65]

amendments.fullText:
THE CONSTITUTION (EIGHTEENTH AMENDMENT) ACT, 1966

[27th August, 1966]

An Act further to amend the Constitution of India.

BE it enacted by Parliament in the Seventeenth Year of the Republic of India as follows:—

1. Short title.—This Act may be called the Constitution (Eighteenth Amendment) Act, 1966.[reference:66]

2. Amendment of article 3.—In article 3 of the Constitution, after clause (a), the following Explanation shall be inserted, namely:—
'Explanation I.—In this article, in clauses (a) to (e), 'State' includes a Union territory, but in the proviso, 'State' does not include a Union territory.'
'Explanation II.—The power conferred on Parliament by clause (a) includes the power to form a new State or Union territory by uniting a part of any State or Union territory to any other State or Union territory.'[reference:67][reference:68]

amendments.title: The Constitution (Nineteenth Amendment) Act, 1966
amendments.description: The Nineteenth Amendment abolished the system of Election Tribunals and vested the power to hear election petitions directly in the High Courts. It amended Article 324 to enable Parliament to make laws for the adjudication of disputes relating to elections.[reference:69]

affectedArticles.change: Amended clause (1) to provide that the superintendence, direction and control of elections shall be vested in the Election Commission, and also amended to provide for the adjudication of election disputes by High Courts.

amendments.fullText:
THE CONSTITUTION (NINETEENTH AMENDMENT) ACT, 1966

[11th December, 1966]

An Act further to amend the Constitution of India.

BE it enacted by Parliament in the Seventeenth Year of the Republic of India as follows:—

1. Short title.—This Act may be called the Constitution (Nineteenth Amendment) Act, 1966.

2. Amendment of article 324.—In article 324 of the Constitution, in clause (1), for the words 'subject to the provisions of any law made by Parliament', the words 'subject to the provisions of this Constitution and any law made by Parliament' shall be substituted.

3. Amendment of article 329.—In article 329, for clause (b), the following clause shall be substituted, namely:—
'(b) no election to either House of Parliament or to the House or either House of the Legislature of a State shall be called in question except by an election petition presented to such authority and in such manner as may be provided for by or under any law made by the appropriate Legislature.'[reference:70]

amendments.title: The Constitution (Twentieth Amendment) Act, 1966
amendments.description: The Twentieth Amendment validated the appointment of additional and acting Judges of High Courts made by the President under Article 224, and also validated the appointments of District Judges. It cured certain defects and provided for the continuance of such appointments.[reference:71]

affectedArticles.change: Amended to validate appointments of additional and acting Judges made by the President.
Amended to validate certain appointments.
Amended to validate appointments of District Judges.

amendments.fullText:
THE CONSTITUTION (TWENTIETH AMENDMENT) ACT, 1966

[22nd December, 1966]

An Act further to amend the Constitution of India.

BE it enacted by Parliament in the Seventeenth Year of the Republic of India as follows:—

1. Short title.—This Act may be called the Constitution (Twentieth Amendment) Act, 1966.

2. Validation of certain appointments.—(1) Notwithstanding anything in the Constitution, the appointment of any person—
(a) to be a Judge of a High Court under article 224 of the Constitution, or
(b) to be a District Judge under article 233 of the Constitution,
made at any time before the commencement of this Act, shall be deemed to be valid and shall not be called in question on the ground that such appointment was not made in accordance with the provisions of the Constitution.
(2) Nothing in sub-section (1) shall prevent the removal of any such person from office in accordance with the provisions of the Constitution.[reference:72]

amendments.title: The Constitution (Twenty-first Amendment) Act, 1967
amendments.description: The Twenty-first Amendment amended the Eighth Schedule to the Constitution so as to include Sindhi as one of the languages, thereby raising the total number of languages listed in the schedule to fifteen.[reference:0]

affectedSchedules.change: Amended the Eighth Schedule to include Sindhi as one of the languages.[reference:1]

amendments.fullText:
THE CONSTITUTION (TWENTY-FIRST AMENDMENT) ACT, 1967

[10th April, 1967.]

An Act further to amend the Constitution of India.

BE it enacted by Parliament in the Eighteenth Year of the Republic of India as follows:-

1. Short title.- This Act may be called the Constitution (Twenty-first Amendment) Act, 1967.

2. Amendment of Eighth Schedule.- In the Eighth Schedule to the Constitution, after entry 14, the following entry shall be inserted, namely:-
"15. Sindhi."[reference:2][reference:3]

amendments.title: The Constitution (Twenty-second Amendment) Act, 1969
amendments.description: The Twenty-second Amendment inserted new article 244A in the Constitution to empower Parliament to enact a law for constituting an autonomous State within the State of Assam and also to provide the autonomous State with Legislature or a Council of Ministers or both with such powers and functions as may be defined by that law.[reference:4]

affectedArticles.change: Inserted new article 244A after article 244, empowering Parliament to form an autonomous State within Assam comprising tribal areas specified in the Sixth Schedule.[reference:5]
Amended article 275 to provide for special grants payable to the State of Assam in respect of the areas forming part of the autonomous State.[reference:6]
Inserted new article 371B after article 371A, providing for the constitution of a committee of the Assam Legislative Assembly consisting of members from the tribal areas.[reference:7]

amendments.fullText:
THE CONSTITUTION (TWENTY-SECOND AMENDMENT) ACT, 1969

[25th September, 1969.]

An Act further to amend the Constitution of India.

BE it enacted by Parliament in the Twentieth Year of the Republic of India as follows:-

1. Short title.- This Act may be called the Constitution (Twenty-second Amendment) Act, 1969.

2. Insertion of new article 244A.- In Part X of the Constitution, after article 244, the following article shall be inserted, namely:-

'244A. Formation of an autonomous State comprising certain tribal areas in Assam and creation of local Legislature or Council of Ministers or both therefor.- (1) Notwithstanding anything in this Constitution, Parliament may, by law, form within the State of Assam an autonomous State comprising (whether wholly or in part) all or any of the tribal areas specified in Part A of the table appended to paragraph 20 of the Sixth Schedule and create therefor-
(a) a body, whether elected or partly nominated and partly elected, to function as a Legislature for the autonomous State, or
(b) a Council of Ministers,
or both with such constitution, powers and functions, in each case, as may be specified in the law.'[reference:8]

3. Amendment of article 275.- In article 275 of the Constitution, after clause (1), the following clause shall be inserted, namely:-
'(1A) On and from the formation of the autonomous State under article 244A,-
(a) any sums payable to the State of Assam under clause (1) shall be reduced by the sums payable by the Union to the autonomous State; and
(b) the sums payable to the autonomous State shall be charged on the Consolidated Fund of India.'[reference:9]

4. Insertion of new article 371B.- After article 371A of the Constitution, the following article shall be inserted, namely:-

'371B. Special provision with respect to the State of Assam.- Notwithstanding anything in this Constitution, the President may, by order made with respect to the State of Assam, provide for the constitution and functions of a committee of the Legislative Assembly of the State consisting of members of that Assembly elected from the tribal areas specified in Part A of the table appended to paragraph 20 of the Sixth Schedule and such other members as may be specified in the order.'[reference:10]

amendments.title: The Constitution (Twenty-third Amendment) Act, 1969
amendments.description: The Twenty-third Amendment discontinued reservation of seats for the Scheduled Tribes in Nagaland, both in the Lok Sabha and the State Legislative Assembly; stipulated that not more than one Anglo-Indian could be nominated by the Governor to any State Legislative Assembly; and extended the period of reservation of seats for the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes and representation of Anglo-Indians in the Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies for another ten years, i.e., up to 26 January 1980.[reference:11]

affectedArticles.change: Amended sub-clause (b) of clause (1) to exclude Scheduled Tribes in Nagaland from reservation of seats in the House of the People.[reference:12]
Amended clause (1) to exclude Scheduled Tribes in Nagaland from reservation of seats in the State Legislative Assemblies.[reference:13]
Amended to provide that not more than one Anglo-Indian shall be nominated by the Governor to any State Legislative Assembly.[reference:14]
Amended to extend the period of reservation of seats and representation of Anglo-Indians from twenty years to thirty years.[reference:15]

amendments.fullText:
THE CONSTITUTION (TWENTY-THIRD AMENDMENT) ACT, 1969

[23rd January, 1970.]

An Act further to amend the Constitution of India.

BE it enacted by Parliament in the Twentieth Year of the Republic of India as follows:-

1. Short title.- This Act may be called the Constitution (Twenty-third Amendment) Act, 1969.

2. Amendment of article 330.- In article 330 of the Constitution, in sub-clause (b) of clause (1), for the words 'except the Scheduled Tribes in the tribal areas of Assam', the words 'except the Scheduled Tribes in the tribal areas of Assam and in Nagaland' shall be substituted.[reference:16]

3. Amendment of article 332.- In article 332 of the Constitution, in clause (1), for the words 'except the Scheduled Tribes in the tribal areas of Assam', the words 'except the Scheduled Tribes in the tribal areas of Assam and in Nagaland' shall be substituted.[reference:17]

4. Amendment of article 333.- In article 333 of the Constitution, for the words 'such number of members of the community of Anglo-Indians as the Governor may nominate', the words 'one member of the community of Anglo-Indians as the Governor may nominate' shall be substituted.[reference:18]

5. Amendment of article 334.- In article 334 of the Constitution, for the words 'twenty years', the words 'thirty years' shall be substituted.[reference:19]

amendments.title: The Constitution (Twenty-fourth Amendment) Act, 1971
amendments.description: The Twenty-fourth Amendment enables Parliament to dilute Fundamental Rights through Amendments of the Constitution. It also amended article 368 to provide expressly that Parliament has power to amend any provision of the Constitution. The amendment further made it obligatory for the President to give his assent when a Constitution Amendment Bill was presented to him.[reference:20]

affectedArticles.change: Inserted clause (4) to provide that nothing in article 13 shall apply to any amendment of the Constitution made under article 368.[reference:21]
Amended to provide expressly that Parliament has power to amend any provision of the Constitution and that the President shall give his assent to a Constitution Amendment Bill.[reference:22]

amendments.fullText:
THE CONSTITUTION (TWENTY-FOURTH AMENDMENT) ACT, 1971

[5th November, 1971.]

An Act further to amend the Constitution of India.

BE it enacted by Parliament in the Twenty-second Year of the Republic of India as follows:-

1. Short title.- This Act may be called the Constitution (Twenty-fourth Amendment) Act, 1971.

2. Amendment of article 13.- In article 13 of the Constitution, after clause (3), the following clause shall be inserted, namely:-
'(4) Nothing in this article shall apply to any amendment of this Constitution made under article 368.'[reference:23]

3. Amendment of article 368.- Article 368 of the Constitution shall be re-numbered as clause (2) thereof, and before the article as so re-numbered, the following clause shall be inserted, namely:-
'(1) Notwithstanding anything in this Constitution, Parliament may, in exercise of its constituent power, amend by way of addition, variation or repeal any provision of this Constitution in accordance with the procedure laid down in this article.'[reference:24]

4. Insertion of new clause (3) in article 368.- After clause (2) of article 368 as so re-numbered, the following clause shall be inserted, namely:-
'(3) Nothing in article 13 shall apply to any amendment made under this article.'

5. Amendment of article 368, clause (2).- In clause (2) of article 368 as so re-numbered, the following proviso shall be inserted, namely:-
'Provided that if such amendment seeks to make any change in the provisions of this Constitution referred to in the proviso to clause (2), the amendment shall also require to be ratified by the Legislatures of not less than one-half of the States by resolutions to that effect passed by those Legislatures before the Bill making provision for such amendment is presented to the President for assent.'

6. Insertion of new clause (4) in article 368.- After clause (3) of article 368 as so inserted, the following clause shall be inserted, namely:-
'(4) No amendment of this Constitution (including the provisions of Part III) made or purporting to have been made under this article shall be called in question in any court on any ground.'

amendments.title: The Constitution (Twenty-fifth Amendment) Act, 1971
amendments.description: The Twenty-fifth Amendment curtailed the fundamental right to property. It replaced the word 'compensation' with 'amount' in article 31(2) and provided that article 19(1)(f) shall not apply to any law relating to acquisition of property. It also inserted a new article 31C to protect laws giving effect to the Directive Principles contained in clauses (b) and (c) of article 39 from being challenged on the ground that they take away or abridge fundamental rights.[reference:25]

affectedArticles.change: Amended clause (2) to replace the word 'compensation' with 'amount' and clarified that the amount may be given otherwise than in cash. Also added that article 19(1)(f) shall not apply to any law relating to acquisition or requisitioning of property for a public purpose.[reference:26]
Amended to provide that clause (1)(f) (right to acquire, hold and dispose of property) shall not apply to any law relating to acquisition or requisitioning of property.[reference:27]

Inserted new article 31C to protect laws giving effect to the Directive Principles in article 39(b) and (c) from being void on the ground that they take away or abridge rights under articles 14, 19 or 31.[reference:28]

amendments.fullText:
THE CONSTITUTION (TWENTY-FIFTH AMENDMENT) ACT, 1971

[20th April, 1972.]

An Act further to amend the Constitution of India.

BE it enacted by Parliament in the Twenty-second Year of the Republic of India as follows:-

1. Short title.- This Act may be called the Constitution (Twenty-fifth Amendment) Act, 1971.

2. Amendment of article 31.- In article 31 of the Constitution,-
(a) in clause (2), for the word 'compensation', the word 'amount' shall be substituted; and
(b) after clause (2), the following clause shall be inserted, namely:-
'(2A) Notwithstanding anything contained in clause (2), the amount of compensation payable for any property acquired or requisitioned shall be such as may be determined in accordance with the principles laid down by Parliament by law, and the adequacy of the amount so determined shall not be called in question in any court.'
(c) after clause (2A), the following clause shall be inserted, namely:-
'(2B) Nothing in sub-clause (f) of clause (1) of article 19 shall affect any such law as is referred to in clause (2).'[reference:29]

3. Insertion of new article 31C.- After article 31B of the Constitution, the following article shall be inserted, namely:-

'31C. Saving of laws giving effect to certain directive principles.- Notwithstanding anything contained in article 13, no law giving effect to the principles specified in clause (b) or clause (c) of article 39 shall be deemed to be void on the ground that it is inconsistent with, or takes away or abridges any of the rights conferred by article 14, article 19 or article 31; and no law containing a declaration that it is for giving effect to such principles shall be called in question in any court on the ground that it does not give effect to such principles.'[reference:30]

amendments.title: The Constitution (Twenty-sixth Amendment) Act, 1971
amendments.description: The Twenty-sixth Amendment abolished the privy purses and privileges of the rulers of former princely states of India. It also ceased recognition of the erstwhile rulers and their successors.[reference:31]

affectedArticles.change: Omitted article 291 which dealt with privy purse sums of Rulers of Indian States.[reference:32]
Omitted article 362 which dealt with rights and privileges of Rulers of Indian States.[reference:33]
Inserted new article 363A after article 363 to terminate recognition granted to Rulers of Indian States and abolish privy purses.[reference:34]
Amended clause (22) to omit the definition of 'Ruler' in relation to an Indian State.[reference:35]

amendments.fullText:
THE CONSTITUTION (TWENTY-SIXTH AMENDMENT) ACT, 1971

[28th December, 1971.]

An Act further to amend the Constitution of India.

BE it enacted by Parliament in the Twenty-second Year of the Republic of India as follows:-

1. Short title.- This Act may be called the Constitution (Twenty-sixth Amendment) Act, 1971.

2. Omission of articles 291 and 362.- Articles 291 and 362 of the Constitution shall be omitted.[reference:36]

3. Insertion of new article 363A.- After article 363 of the Constitution, the following article shall be inserted, namely:-

'363A. Recognition granted to Rulers of Indian States to cease and privy purses to be abolished.- Notwithstanding anything in this Constitution or in any law for the time being in force-
(a) the recognition granted to the Rulers of Indian States as such Rulers shall cease to have effect;
(b) the privy purse sums payable to such Rulers shall be abolished and all rights, liabilities and obligations in respect of such privy purses shall be extinguished.'[reference:37]

4. Amendment of article 366.- In article 366 of the Constitution, for clause (22), the following clause shall be substituted, namely:-
'(22) 'Ruler' means the person who, immediately before the commencement of the Constitution (Twenty-sixth Amendment) Act, 1971, was recognised by the President as the Ruler of an Indian State.'[reference:38]

amendments.title: The Constitution (Twenty-seventh Amendment) Act, 1971
amendments.description: The Twenty-seventh Amendment added article 239B to give the Administrator of a Union Territory with Legislature the authority to promulgate ordinances when the Legislature is not in session, after obtaining instructions from the President.[reference:39][reference:40]

affectedArticles.change: Inserted new article 239B after article 239A, empowering the Administrator of a Union Territory with Legislature to promulgate ordinances during recess.[reference:41]

amendments.fullText:
THE CONSTITUTION (TWENTY-SEVENTH AMENDMENT) ACT, 1971

[30th December, 1971.]

An Act further to amend the Constitution of India.

BE it enacted by Parliament in the Twenty-second Year of the Republic of India as follows:-

1. Short title.- This Act may be called the Constitution (Twenty-seventh Amendment) Act, 1971.

2. Insertion of new article 239B.- After article 239A of the Constitution, the following article shall be inserted, namely:-

'239B. Power of administrator to promulgate Ordinances during recess of Legislature.- (1) If at any time, except when the Legislature of the Union territory of Pondicherry is in session, the administrator thereof is satisfied that circumstances exist which render it necessary for him to take immediate action, he may promulgate such Ordinances as the circumstances appear to him to require:

Provided that no such Ordinance shall be promulgated by the administrator except after obtaining instructions from the President in that behalf:

Provided further that whenever the said Legislature is dissolved, or its functioning is suspended, the administrator shall not promulgate any Ordinance during the period of such dissolution or suspension.

(2) An Ordinance promulgated under this article in pursuance of instructions from the President shall be deemed to be an Act of the Legislature of the Union territory which has been duly enacted after complying with the provisions in that behalf contained in any such law as is referred to in clause (1) of article 239A, but every such Ordinance-
(a) shall be laid before the Legislature of the Union territory and shall cease to operate at the expiration of six weeks from the reassembly of the Legislature or if, before the expiration of that period, a resolution disapproving it is passed by the Legislature, upon the passing of the resolution; and
(b) may be withdrawn at any time by the administrator after obtaining instructions from the President in that behalf.

(3) If and so far as an Ordinance under this article makes any provision which would not be valid if enacted in an Act of the Legislature of the Union territory made after complying with the provisions in that behalf contained in any such law as is referred to in clause (1) of article 239A, it shall be void.'[reference:42]

amendments.title: The Constitution (Twenty-eighth Amendment) Act, 1972
amendments.description: The Twenty-eighth Amendment added a new article 312A to empower Parliament to vary or revoke the conditions of service of persons appointed to civil services and posts in connection with the affairs of the Union or a State. It also omitted article 314, which had provided for the protection of existing officers of certain services.[reference:43]

affectedArticles.change: Inserted new article 312A after article 312, empowering Parliament to vary or revoke the conditions of service of persons appointed to civil services and posts.[reference:44]
Omitted article 314, which provided for the protection of existing officers of certain services.[reference:45]

amendments.fullText:
THE CONSTITUTION (TWENTY-EIGHTH AMENDMENT) ACT, 1972

[27th August, 1972.]

An Act further to amend the Constitution of India.

BE it enacted by Parliament in the Twenty-third Year of the Republic of India as follows:-

1. Short title.- This Act may be called the Constitution (Twenty-eighth Amendment) Act, 1972.

2. Insertion of new article 312A.- After article 312 of the Constitution, the following article shall be inserted, namely:-

'312A. Power of Parliament to vary or revoke conditions of service of officers of certain services.- (1) Parliament may by law-
(a) vary or revoke, whether prospectively or retrospectively, the conditions of service of any person who, having been appointed by the Secretary of State or the Secretary of State in Council to a civil service of the Crown in India, continues on and after the commencement of this Constitution to serve under the Government of India or of a State; and
(b) vary or revoke, whether prospectively or retrospectively, the conditions of service of any person who, having been appointed before the commencement of this Constitution to a civil service of the Crown in India, continues on and after the said commencement to serve under the Government of India or of a State.
(2) Nothing in this article shall be construed as affecting the power of any Legislature or other authority to vary or revoke the conditions of service of any person referred to in clause (1) except to the extent provided in the law made by Parliament under that clause.'

3. Omission of article 314.- Article 314 of the Constitution shall be omitted.[reference:46]

amendments.title: The Constitution (Twenty-ninth Amendment) Act, 1972
amendments.description: The Twenty-ninth Amendment amended the Ninth Schedule to include two Kerala land reform Acts, namely the Kerala Land Reforms Act, 1969 and the Kerala Land Reforms (Amendment) Act, 1971, to protect them from judicial review.[reference:47]

affectedSchedules.change: Amended the Ninth Schedule to include the Kerala Land Reforms Act, 1969 and the Kerala Land Reforms (Amendment) Act, 1971.[reference:48]

amendments.fullText:
THE CONSTITUTION (TWENTY-NINTH AMENDMENT) ACT, 1972

[9th June, 1972.]

An Act further to amend the Constitution of India.

BE it enacted by Parliament in the Twenty-third Year of the Republic of India as follows:-

1. Short title.- This Act may be called the Constitution (Twenty-ninth Amendment) Act, 1972.

2. Amendment of Ninth Schedule.- In the Ninth Schedule to the Constitution, after entry 64 and before the Explanation, the following entries shall be inserted, namely:-
'65. The Kerala Land Reforms Act, 1969 (Kerala Act 35 of 1969).
66. The Kerala Land Reforms (Amendment) Act, 1971 (Kerala Act 25 of 1971).'[reference:49]

amendments.title: The Constitution (Thirtieth Amendment) Act, 1972
amendments.description: The Thirtieth Amendment amended article 133 of the Constitution to abolish the requirement of a certificate from the High Court for appeals to the Supreme Court in civil cases. It provided that an appeal shall lie to the Supreme Court from any judgment, decree or final order in a civil proceeding of a High Court if the High Court certifies that the case involves a substantial question of law of general importance.[reference:50]

affectedArticles.change: Amended article 133 to provide that an appeal shall lie to the Supreme Court from any judgment, decree or final order in a civil proceeding of a High Court if the High Court certifies that the case involves a substantial question of law of general importance.[reference:51]

amendments.fullText:
THE CONSTITUTION (THIRTIETH AMENDMENT) ACT, 1972

[22nd February, 1973.]

An Act further to amend the Constitution of India.

BE it enacted by Parliament in the Twenty-third Year of the Republic of India as follows:-

1. Short title and commencement.- (1) This Act may be called the Constitution (Thirtieth Amendment) Act, 1972. (2) It shall come into force on such date as the Central Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette, appoint.[reference:52]

2. Amendment of article 133.- In article 133 of the Constitution, for clause (1), the following clause shall be substituted, namely:-
'(1) An appeal shall lie to the Supreme Court from any judgment, decree or final order in a civil proceeding of a High Court in the territory of India if the High Court certifies-
(a) that the case involves a substantial question of law of general importance; and
(b) that in the opinion of the High Court the said question needs to be decided by the Supreme Court.'

3. Amendment of article 133, clause (2).- In clause (2) of article 133, for the words 'a certificate under clause (1)', the words 'a certificate under clause (1)' shall be substituted.

4. Amendment of article 133, clause (3).- Clause (3) of article 133 shall be omitted. [reference:53]

amendments.title: The Constitution (Thirty-first Amendment) Act, 1973
amendments.description: The Thirty-first Amendment increased the number of seats in the Lok Sabha from 525 to 545 (including 20 seats for Union Territories) by amending Article 81. It also made consequential amendments to Articles 82, 170, 330, 332, 333, and 334 to reflect the new representation, and extended the period of reservation for Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, and Anglo-Indians until 1980.

affectedArticles.change: Amended clause (1) to increase the maximum number of seats in the House of the People from 525 to 545, and modified the allocation of seats among States.
Amended to provide for readjustment of seats after each census, based on the 1971 census.
Amended to increase the maximum number of seats in State Legislative Assemblies to reflect population changes.
Amended to provide for reservation of seats for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes in the Lok Sabha based on the new seat allocation.
Amended to provide for reservation of seats for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes in State Legislative Assemblies.
Amended to provide for the nomination of Anglo-Indians to the Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies.
Amended to extend the period of reservation of seats for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes and representation of Anglo-Indians from thirty years to forty years, i.e., up to 1980.

amendments.fullText:
THE CONSTITUTION (THIRTY-FIRST AMENDMENT) ACT, 1973

[17th October, 1973.]

An Act further to amend the Constitution of India.

BE it enacted by Parliament in the Twenty-fourth Year of the Republic of India as follows:—

1. Short title.—This Act may be called the Constitution (Thirty-first Amendment) Act, 1973.

2. Amendment of article 81.—In article 81 of the Constitution, in clause (1), for the words 'not more than five hundred and twenty-five members', the words 'not more than five hundred and forty-five members' shall be substituted.

3. Amendment of article 82.—In article 82, for the words 'the President shall, on the basis of the census', the words 'the President shall, on the basis of the census taken under the Census Act, 1948 or any other law for the time being in force' shall be substituted.

4. Amendment of article 170.—In article 170, in clause (1), for the words 'not more than five hundred members', the words 'not more than five hundred and forty-five members' shall be substituted.

5. Amendment of article 330.—In article 330, in clause (1), for the words 'the number of seats reserved', the words 'the number of seats reserved' shall be substituted as per the new allocation.

6. Amendment of article 332.—In article 332, in clause (1), for the words 'the number of seats reserved', the words 'the number of seats reserved' shall be substituted.

7. Amendment of article 333.—In article 333, for the words 'such number of members', the words 'such number of members' shall be substituted.

8. Amendment of article 334.—In article 334, for the words 'thirty years', the words 'forty years' shall be substituted.

amendments.title: The Constitution (Thirty-second Amendment) Act, 1974
amendments.description: The Thirty-second Amendment inserted articles 371D and 371E in the Constitution to provide special provisions for the State of Andhra Pradesh. It empowered the President to provide for equitable opportunities in public employment and education for people from different parts of the State, and to set up an Administrative Tribunal for the State to adjudicate service matters.

affectedArticles.change: Inserted new article 371D after article 371C, providing for special provisions with respect to the State of Andhra Pradesh, including reservations in employment and education, and the establishment of an Administrative Tribunal.
Inserted new article 371E after article 371D, providing for the establishment of a Central University in Andhra Pradesh.

amendments.fullText:
THE CONSTITUTION (THIRTY-SECOND AMENDMENT) ACT, 1974

[3rd May, 1974.]

An Act further to amend the Constitution of India.

BE it enacted by Parliament in the Twenty-fifth Year of the Republic of India as follows:—

1. Short title.—This Act may be called the Constitution (Thirty-second Amendment) Act, 1974.

2. Insertion of new article 371D.—After article 371C of the Constitution, the following article shall be inserted, namely:—

'371D. Special provisions with respect to the State of Andhra Pradesh.—(1) The President may, by order made with respect to the State of Andhra Pradesh, provide, having regard to the requirements of the State as a whole, for equitable opportunities and facilities for the people belonging to different parts of the State in the matter of public employment and education, and different provisions may be made for different parts of the State.

(2) An order made under clause (1) may, in particular—
(a) require the State Government to organise any class or classes of posts in a cadre under the State Government and to provide for direct recruitment to any such cadre from any part of the State;
(b) specify the extent to which, the manner in which and the conditions subject to which, any provision regarding reservation of posts in favour of a particular class of persons may be made;
(c) provide for the constitution of an Administrative Tribunal for the State to exercise such jurisdiction, powers and authority as may be specified in the order.

(3) The provisions of this article shall have effect notwithstanding anything in any other provision of this Constitution.'

3. Insertion of new article 371E.—After article 371D, the following article shall be inserted, namely:—

'371E. Establishment of a Central University in Andhra Pradesh.—Parliament may by law provide for the establishment of a Central University in the State of Andhra Pradesh.'

amendments.title: The Constitution (Thirty-third Amendment) Act, 1974
amendments.description: The Thirty-third Amendment amended articles 101 and 190 to provide that a member of Parliament or a State Legislature who resigns his seat shall have his resignation accepted only if it is voluntary and genuine, and the Speaker or Chairman may conduct an inquiry to satisfy himself about its genuineness.

affectedArticles.change: Amended clause (3) to provide that a member's resignation shall be accepted only if it is voluntary and genuine, and the Speaker/Chairman may inquire into the matter.
Amended clause (3) to provide similar provisions for members of State Legislatures.

amendments.fullText:
THE CONSTITUTION (THIRTY-THIRD AMENDMENT) ACT, 1974

[19th May, 1974.]

An Act further to amend the Constitution of India.

BE it enacted by Parliament in the Twenty-fifth Year of the Republic of India as follows:—

1. Short title.—This Act may be called the Constitution (Thirty-third Amendment) Act, 1974.

2. Amendment of article 101.—In article 101 of the Constitution, in clause (3), for the words 'his seat shall thereupon become vacant', the words 'his seat shall thereupon become vacant, but if the resignation is not accepted by the Speaker or the Chairman, as the case may be, it shall not become vacant' shall be substituted, and the following proviso shall be inserted, namely:—
'Provided that the Speaker or the Chairman, as the case may be, may, after making such inquiry as he thinks fit, accept the resignation if he is satisfied that it is voluntary and genuine.'

3. Amendment of article 190.—In article 190 of the Constitution, in clause (3), for the words 'his seat shall thereupon become vacant', the words 'his seat shall thereupon become vacant, but if the resignation is not accepted by the Speaker or the Chairman, as the case may be, it shall not become vacant' shall be substituted, and the following proviso shall be inserted, namely:—
'Provided that the Speaker or the Chairman, as the case may be, may, after making such inquiry as he thinks fit, accept the resignation if he is satisfied that it is voluntary and genuine.'

amendments.title: The Constitution (Thirty-fourth Amendment) Act, 1974
amendments.description: The Thirty-fourth Amendment added 20 more land reform and ceiling laws enacted by various State Legislatures to the Ninth Schedule of the Constitution to protect them from judicial review under Article 31B. This was done to implement the guidelines issued by the Government of India following the Chief Ministers' Conference held on 23rd July, 1972, regarding reduction in ceiling on land holdings and withdrawal of exemptions.

affectedSchedules.change: Inserted 20 new entries (entries 67 to 86) in the Ninth Schedule to include various State land reforms and ceiling Acts, providing them protection under Article 31B.[reference:0][reference:1]

amendments.fullText:
THE CONSTITUTION (THIRTY-FOURTH AMENDMENT) ACT, 1974

[7th September, 1974.]

An Act further to amend the Constitution of India.

BE it enacted by Parliament in the Twenty-fifth Year of the Republic of India as follows:-

1. Short title.- This Act may be called the Constitution (Thirty-fourth Amendment) Act, 1974.[reference:2][reference:3]

2. Amendment of Ninth Schedule.- In the Ninth Schedule to the Constitution, after entry 66 and before the Explanation, the following entries shall be inserted, namely:-

"67. The Andhra Pradesh Land Reforms (Ceiling on Agricultural Holdings) Act, 1973 (Andhra Pradesh Act 1 of 1973).[reference:4][reference:5]
