affectedArticles.change: Amended to empower Parliament to restrict or abrogate the Fundamental Rights of persons serving in the armed forces, the paramilitary forces, and intelligence organisations in the interests of the proper discharge of their duties and the maintenance of discipline.

amendments.fullText:
THE CONSTITUTION (FIFTIETH AMENDMENT) ACT, 1984

[11th September, 1984.]

An Act further to amend the Constitution of India.

BE it enacted by Parliament in the Thirty-fifth Year of the Republic of India as follows:—

1. Short title.—This Act may be called the Constitution (Fiftieth Amendment) Act, 1984.

2. Amendment of article 33.—In article 33 of the Constitution, for the words 'members of the Armed Forces', the words 'members of the Armed Forces or the forces charged with the maintenance of public order or intelligence organisations' shall be substituted, and for the words 'in the interests of the proper discharge of their duties', the words 'in the interests of the proper discharge of their duties and the maintenance of discipline' shall be substituted.

amendments.title: The Constitution (Fifty-first Amendment) Act, 1984
amendments.description: The Fifty-first Amendment provided for reservation of seats for Scheduled Tribes in the Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies in the autonomous districts of Assam, while removing such reservation for Scheduled Tribes in Nagaland and Meghalaya. It amended Articles 330 and 332 of the Constitution to give effect to this change.

affectedArticles.change: In clause (1), sub-clause (b) was substituted to provide for reservation of seats for Scheduled Tribes in the Lok Sabha, except the Scheduled Tribes in the autonomous districts of Assam.[reference:0]

In clause (1), the words 'except the Scheduled Tribes in the tribal areas of Assam, in Nagaland and in Meghalaya' were substituted with 'except the Scheduled Tribes in the autonomous districts of Assam'.[reference:1]

amendments.fullText:
THE CONSTITUTION (FIFTY-FIRST AMENDMENT) ACT, 1984

[29th April, 1985.]

An Act further to amend the Constitution of India.

BE it enacted by Parliament in the Thirty-fifth Year of the Republic of India as follows:—

1. Short title and commencement.—(1) This Act may be called the Constitution (Fifty-first Amendment) Act, 1984. (2) It shall come into force on such date as the Central Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette, appoint.

2. Amendment of article 330.—(1) In article 330 of the Constitution, in clause (1), for sub-clause (b), the following sub-clause shall be substituted, namely:—
'(b) the Scheduled Tribes, except the Scheduled Tribes in the autonomous districts of Assam; and'.

(2) The amendment made to article 330 of the Constitution by sub-section (1) shall not affect any representation in the House of the People until the dissolution of the House of the People existing at the commencement of this Act.

3. Amendment of article 332.—(1) In article 332 of the Constitution, in clause (1), for the words 'except the Scheduled Tribes in the tribal areas of Assam, in Nagaland and in Meghalaya', the words 'except the Scheduled Tribes in the autonomous districts of Assam' shall be substituted.

(2) The amendment made to article 332 of the Constitution by sub-section (1) shall not affect any representation in the Legislative Assembly of the State of Nagaland or the Legislative Assembly of the State of Meghalaya until the dissolution of the Legislative Assembly of the State of Nagaland or the Legislative Assembly of the State of Meghalaya existing at the commencement of this Act.[reference:2]

amendments.title: The Constitution (Fifty-second Amendment) Act, 1985
amendments.description: Popularly known as the Anti-Defection Law, the Fifty-second Amendment inserted the Tenth Schedule in the Constitution to curb the evil of political defections. It laid down provisions for disqualification of elected and nominated members of Parliament and State Legislatures on grounds of defection to another political party. The Amendment also introduced the word 'Political Party' in the Constitution and amended Articles 101, 102, 190 and 191 to give effect to the anti-defection provisions.

affectedArticles.change: Amended sub-clause (a) of clause (3) to refer to clause (1) or clause (2) of article 102, thereby incorporating the new disqualification grounds introduced by the Tenth Schedule.[reference:0]
Amended to include clause (2) which provides that a person shall be disqualified for being a member of either House of Parliament if he is so disqualified under the Tenth Schedule.[reference:1]
Amended to incorporate the disqualification provisions of the Tenth Schedule for members of State Legislatures.[reference:2]

Amended to include clause (2) which provides that a person shall be disqualified for being a member of the Legislative Assembly or Legislative Council of a State if he is so disqualified under the Tenth Schedule.[reference:3][reference:4]

affectedSchedules.change: Inserted the Tenth Schedule containing provisions as to disqualification on ground of defection. The Schedule sets out the grounds for disqualification of members of Parliament and State Legislatures, including voluntary relinquishment of party membership, voting contrary to party direction, and joining another political party. It also provides for exceptions in cases of splits and mergers of political parties, and empowers the presiding officer to decide questions of disqualification.[reference:5][reference:6][reference:7]

amendments.fullText:
THE CONSTITUTION (FIFTY-SECOND AMENDMENT) ACT, 1985

[15th February, 1985.]

An Act further to amend the Constitution of India.

BE it enacted by Parliament in the Thirty-sixth Year of the Republic of India as follows:—

1. Short title and commencement.—(1) This Act may be called the Constitution (Fifty-second Amendment) Act, 1985. (2) It shall come into force on such date as the Central Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette, appoint.[reference:8]

2. Amendment of article 101.—In article 101 of the Constitution, in sub-clause (a) of clause (3), for the words, brackets and figures 'clause (1) of article 102', the words, brackets and figures 'clause (1) or clause (2) of article 102' shall be substituted.[reference:9]

3. Amendment of article 102.—In article 102 of the Constitution, after clause (1), the following clause shall be inserted, namely:—
'(2) A person shall be disqualified for being a member of either House of Parliament if he is so disqualified under the Tenth Schedule.'[reference:10]

4. Amendment of article 190.—In article 190 of the Constitution, in sub-clause (a) of clause (3), for the words, brackets and figures 'clause (1) of article 191', the words, brackets and figures 'clause (1) or clause (2) of article 191' shall be substituted.

5. Amendment of article 191.—In article 191 of the Constitution, after clause (1), the following clause shall be inserted, namely:—
'(2) A person shall be disqualified for being a member of the Legislative Assembly or Legislative Council of a State if he is so disqualified under the Tenth Schedule.'[reference:11]

6. Insertion of Tenth Schedule.—After the Ninth Schedule to the Constitution, the following Schedule shall be inserted, namely:—

'TENTH SCHEDULE
[Articles 102(2) and 191(2)]

Provisions as to disqualification on ground of defection

1. Interpretation.—In this Schedule, unless the context otherwise requires,—
(a) 'House' means either House of Parliament or the Legislative Assembly or, as the case may be, either House of the Legislature of a State;
(b) 'legislature party' means a group consisting of all the members of that House belonging to any political party in accordance with the provisions of paragraph 3;
(c) 'original political party', in relation to a member of a House, means the political party to which he belongs for the purposes of sub-paragraph (1) of paragraph 2;
(d) 'political party' means a political party registered under the Representation of the People Act, 1951.

2. Disqualification on ground of defection.—(1) Subject to the provisions of paragraphs 4 and 5, a member of a House belonging to any political party shall be disqualified for being a member of the House—
(a) if he has voluntarily given up his membership of such political party; or
(b) if he votes or abstains from voting in such House contrary to any direction issued by the political party to which he belongs or by any person or authority authorised by it in this behalf, without obtaining, in either case, the prior permission of such political party, person or authority and such voting or abstention has not been condoned by such political party, person or authority within fifteen days from the date of such voting or abstention.

Explanation.—For the purposes of this sub-paragraph,—
(a) an elected member of a House shall be deemed to belong to the political party, if any, by which he was set up as a candidate for election as such member;
(b) a nominated member of a House shall,—
(i) where he is a member of any political party on the date of his nomination as such member, be deemed to belong to such political party;
(ii) in any other case, be deemed to belong to the political party of which he becomes, or, as the case may be, first becomes, a member before the expiry of six months from the date on which he takes his seat after complying with the requirements of article 99 or, as the case may be, article 188.[reference:12]

(2) A member of a House shall be disqualified for being a member of the House if he is a nominated member of that House and he has become a member of any political party after the expiry of six months from the date on which he takes his seat after complying with the requirements of article 99 or, as the case may be, article 188.

(3) A member of a House shall not be disqualified under this paragraph if he has been elected to the House as a candidate set up by a political party and he, by reason of his being a member of a committee or body specified in the rules made by the Chairman or the Speaker, as the case may be, is required to exercise any power or perform any duty which involves voting or abstaining from voting in the House, and such voting or abstention is not contrary to the direction issued by the political party.

(4) A member of a House shall not be disqualified under this paragraph if he is a member of a political party and he has been elected to the House as a candidate set up by such political party and he, by reason of his being a member of a committee or body specified in the rules made by the Chairman or the Speaker, as the case may be, is required to exercise any power or perform any duty which involves voting or abstaining from voting in the House, and such voting or abstention is not contrary to the direction issued by the political party.

3. Exceptions.—(1) A member of a House shall not be disqualified under paragraph 2 where—
(a) he has voluntarily given up his membership of his original political party, and such original political party has not been recognised as a political party in that House; or
(b) his original political party has merged with another political party, and he claims that he and any other members of his original political party—
(i) have become members of the other political party or, as the case may be, of the new political party formed by such merger; or
(ii) have not accepted the merger and have opted to function as a separate group.

(2) For the purposes of sub-paragraph (1),—
(a) a merger of the original political party of a member of a House shall be deemed to have taken place if not less than two-thirds of the members of the legislature party concerned have agreed to such merger;
(b) a member of a House shall be deemed to have voluntarily given up his membership of his original political party if he has joined any other political party after the expiration of six months from the date on which he takes his seat.

4. Disqualification on ground of defection for independent members.—A member of a House who has been elected as an independent candidate shall be disqualified for being a member of the House if he joins any political party after his election.

5. Disqualification on ground of defection for nominated members.—A member of a House who has been nominated to the House shall be disqualified for being a member of the House if he joins any political party after the expiry of six months from the date on which he takes his seat.

6. Decision on questions of disqualification.—(1) If any question arises as to whether a member of a House has become subject to disqualification under this Schedule, the question shall be referred for the decision of the Chairman or, as the case may be, the Speaker of such House and his decision shall be final.
(2) Where the question referred to in sub-paragraph (1) relates to the Chairman or the Speaker, it shall be decided by a member of the House elected by the House in that behalf and his decision shall be final.
(3) In deciding any question under this Schedule, the Chairman or the Speaker, or the member elected under sub-paragraph (2), shall have all the powers of a civil court for the purposes of summoning and enforcing the attendance of witnesses, production of documents, and the like.

7. Rules.—(1) Subject to the provisions of sub-paragraph (2), the Chairman or the Speaker of a House may make rules for giving effect to the provisions of this Schedule, and in particular, and without prejudice to the generality of the foregoing, such rules may provide for—
(a) the maintenance of registers or other records as to the political parties, if any, to which different members of the House belong;
(b) the report which the leader of a legislature party in relation to a member of a House shall furnish with regard to any condonation of the nature referred to in clause (b) of sub-paragraph (1) of paragraph 2 in respect of such member, the time within which and the authority to whom such report shall be furnished;
(c) the reports, which a political party shall furnish with regard to admission to such political party of any members of the House and the officer of the House to whom such reports shall be furnished; and
(d) the procedure for deciding any question referred to in sub-paragraph (1) of paragraph 6 including the procedure for any inquiry which may be made for the purpose of deciding such question.[reference:13]

(2) The rules made by the Chairman or the Speaker of a House under sub-paragraph (1) shall be laid as soon as may be after they are made before the House for a total period of thirty days which may be comprised in one session or in two or more successive sessions and shall take effect upon the expiry of the said period of thirty days unless they are sooner approved with or without modifications or disapproved by the House and where they are so approved, they shall take effect on such approval in the form in which they were laid or in such modified form, as the case may be, and where they are so disapproved, they shall be of no effect.[reference:14]

(3) The Chairman or the Speaker of a House may, without prejudice to the provisions of article 105 or, as the case may be, article 194, and to any other power which he may have under this Constitution direct that   any wilful contravention by any person of the rules made under this paragraph may be dealt with in the same manner as a breach of privilege of the House.[reference:15]

8. Bar of jurisdiction of courts.—Notwithstanding anything in this Constitution, no court shall have any jurisdiction in respect of any matter connected with the disqualification of a member of a House under this Schedule.

9. Powers of the Chairman and Speaker.—For the purposes of this Schedule, the Chairman and the Speaker of a House shall have the same powers as are vested in a court under the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, in respect of the following matters, namely:—
(a) the summoning and enforcing the attendance of any person and examining him on oath;
(b) the requiring the discovery and production of any document;
(c) the receiving of evidence on affidavits;
(d) the issuing of any commission for the examination of witnesses.'

amendments.title: The Constitution (Fifty-third Amendment) Act, 1986
amendments.description: The Fifty-third Amendment inserted a new Article 371G in the Constitution to confer special provisions for the State of Mizoram. This amendment was enacted following the Memorandum of Settlement on Mizoram signed on 30 June 1986, which envisaged the conferment of statehood on the Union territory of Mizoram. Article 371G provides that no Act of Parliament relating to religious or social practices of the Mizos, Mizo customary law and procedure, administration of justice according to Mizo customary law, and ownership and transfer of land shall apply to Mizoram unless the State Legislative Assembly so decides. It also stipulates that the Mizoram Legislative Assembly shall consist of not less than forty members.

affectedArticles.change: Inserted new Article 371G after Article 371F, providing special provisions for the State of Mizoram regarding exemption from Central laws on Mizo social and customary matters, and specifying a minimum of forty members for the Mizoram Legislative Assembly.

newArticles.change: Inserted to provide special provisions for the State of Mizoram, exempting it from certain Central laws relating to Mizo social and customary practices, and specifying the minimum strength of the Mizoram Legislative Assembly.

amendments.fullText:
THE CONSTITUTION (FIFTY-THIRD AMENDMENT) ACT, 1986

[14th August, 1986.]

An Act further to amend the Constitution of India.

BE it enacted by Parliament in the Thirty-seventh Year of the Republic of India as follows:—

1. Short title and commencement.—(1) This Act may be called the Constitution (Fifty-third Amendment) Act, 1986. (2) It shall come into force on such date as the Central Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette, appoint.

2. Insertion of new article 371G.—After article 371F of the Constitution, the following article shall be inserted, namely:—

'371G. Special provision with respect to the State of Mizoram.—Notwithstanding anything in this Constitution,-
(a) no Act of Parliament in respect of-
(i) religious or social practices of the Mizos,
(ii) Mizo customary law and procedure,
(iii) administration of civil and criminal justice involving decisions according to Mizo customary law,
(iv) ownership and transfer of land,
shall apply to the State of Mizoram unless the Legislative Assembly of the State of Mizoram by a resolution so decides:
Provided that nothing in this clause shall apply to any Central Act in force in the Union territory of Mizoram immediately before the commencement of this Act;
(b) the Legislative Assembly of the State of Mizoram shall consist of not less than forty members.'

amendments.title: The Constitution (Fifty-fourth Amendment) Act, 1986
amendments.description: The Fifty-fourth Amendment substantially increased the salaries of Judges of the Supreme Court and High Courts to address the impact of inflation and attract the best legal talent to the judiciary. It amended Articles 125 and 221 to empower Parliament to determine the salaries of Judges by law, and revised the salary figures in Part D of the Second Schedule. The salaries of the Chief Justice of India were raised from Rs. 5,000 to Rs. 10,000 per month; Judges of the Supreme Court from Rs. 4,000 to Rs. 9,000; Chief Justices of High Courts from Rs. 4,000 to Rs. 9,000; and Judges of High Courts from Rs. 3,500 to Rs. 8,000 per month.

affectedArticles.change: Substituted clause (1) to provide that the salaries of Judges of the Supreme Court shall be determined by Parliament by law, and until such provision is made, the salaries as specified in the Second Schedule shall apply.

Substituted clause (1) to provide that the salaries of Judges of each High Court shall be determined by Parliament by law, and until such provision is made, the salaries as specified in the Second Schedule shall apply.

affectedSchedules.change: Amended Part D of the Second Schedule to increase the salaries of Judges: Chief Justice of India from Rs. 5,000 to Rs. 10,000 per month; Judges of the Supreme Court from Rs. 4,000 to Rs. 9,000; Chief Justices of High Courts from Rs. 4,000 to Rs. 9,000; and Judges of High Courts from Rs. 3,500 to Rs. 8,000 per month.

amendments.fullText:
THE CONSTITUTION (FIFTY-FOURTH AMENDMENT) ACT, 1986

[14th March, 1987.]

An Act further to amend the Constitution of India.

BE it enacted by Parliament in the Thirty-seventh Year of the Republic of India as follows:—

1. Short title and commencement.—(1) This Act may be called the Constitution (Fifty-fourth Amendment) Act, 1986. (2) It shall be deemed to have come into force on the 1st day of April, 1986.

2. Amendment of article 125.—In article 125 of the Constitution, for clause (1), the following clause shall be substituted, namely:—
'(1) There shall be paid to the Judges of the Supreme Court such salaries as may be determined by Parliament by law and, until provision in that behalf is so made, such salaries as are specified in the Second Schedule.'

3. Amendment of article 221.—In article 221 of the Constitution, for clause (1), the following clause shall be substituted, namely:—
'(1) There shall be paid to the Judges of each High Court such salaries as may be determined by Parliament by law and, until provision in that behalf is so made, such salaries as are specified in the Second Schedule.'

4. Amendment of Second Schedule.—In the Second Schedule to the Constitution, in Part D,—
(a) in sub-paragraph (1) of paragraph 9, (i) for the figures and word '5,000 rupees', the figures and word '10,000 rupees' shall be substituted; (ii) for the figures and word '4,000 rupees', the figures and word '9,000 rupees' shall be substituted;
(b) in sub-paragraph (1) of paragraph 10, (i) for the figures and word '4,000 rupees', the figures and word '9,000 rupees' shall be substituted; (ii) for the figures and word '3,500 rupees', the figures and word '8,000 rupees' shall be substituted.

amendments.title: The Constitution (Fifty-fifth Amendment) Act, 1986
amendments.description: The Fifty-fifth Amendment conferred statehood on Arunachal Pradesh while providing special constitutional safeguards for the new State. It inserted Article 371H to grant the Governor of Arunachal Pradesh special responsibility with respect to law and order, exercisable in his individual judgment after consulting the Council of Ministers, until the President directs otherwise. The amendment also provided that the Legislative Assembly of Arunachal Pradesh shall consist of not less than thirty members.

newArticles.title: Special provision with respect to the State of Arunachal Pradesh
newArticles.change: Inserted new Article 371H providing special responsibility to the Governor with respect to law and order and prescribing that the Legislative Assembly of Arunachal Pradesh shall consist of not less than thirty members.

amendments.fullText:
THE CONSTITUTION (FIFTY-FIFTH AMENDMENT) ACT, 1986

[20th February, 1987.]

An Act further to amend the Constitution of India.

BE it enacted by Parliament in the Thirty-seventh Year of the Republic of India as follows:—

1. Short title and commencement.—(1) This Act may be called the Constitution (Fifty-fifth Amendment) Act, 1986.

(2) It shall come into force on such date as the Central Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette, appoint.

2. Insertion of new article 371H.—After article 371G of the Constitution, the following article shall be inserted, namely:—

'371H. Special provision with respect to the State of Arunachal Pradesh.—Notwithstanding anything in this Constitution,—
(a) the Governor of Arunachal Pradesh shall have special responsibility with respect to law and order in the State of Arunachal Pradesh and in the discharge of his functions in relation thereto, the Governor shall, after consulting the Council of Ministers, exercise his individual judgment as to the action to be taken:

Provided that if any question arises whether any matter is or is not a matter as respects which the Governor is under this clause required to act in the exercise of his individual judgment, the decision of the Governor in his discretion shall be final, and the validity of anything done by the Governor shall not be called in question on the ground that he ought or ought not to have acted in the exercise of his individual judgment:

Provided further that if the President, on receipt of a report from the Governor or otherwise, is satisfied that it is no longer necessary for the Governor to have special responsibility with respect to law and order in the State of Arunachal Pradesh, he may, by order, direct that the Governor shall cease to have such special responsibility from such date as may be specified in the order;

(b) the Legislative Assembly of the State of Arunachal Pradesh shall consist of not less than thirty members.'

amendments.title: The Constitution (Fifty-sixth Amendment) Act, 1987
amendments.description: The Fifty-sixth Amendment conferred statehood on Goa while continuing Daman and Diu as a Union Territory. It amended the First Schedule to include the State of Goa and the Union Territory of Daman and Diu separately, amended the Fourth Schedule to provide representation for Goa in the Council of States (Rajya Sabha), and inserted Article 371I to provide that the Legislative Assembly of the State of Goa shall consist of not less than thirty members.

newArticles.title: Special provision with respect to the State of Goa
newArticles.change: Inserted new Article 371I providing that the Legislative Assembly of the State of Goa shall consist of not less than thirty members.

affectedSchedules.change: Amended the First Schedule to include Goa as a State and to constitute Daman and Diu as a separate Union Territory.
Amended the Fourth Schedule to provide representation for the State of Goa in the Council of States (Rajya Sabha).

amendments.fullText:
THE CONSTITUTION (FIFTY-SIXTH AMENDMENT) ACT, 1987

[30th May, 1987.]

An Act further to amend the Constitution of India.

BE it enacted by Parliament in the Thirty-eighth Year of the Republic of India as follows:—

1. Short title and commencement.—(1) This Act may be called the Constitution (Fifty-sixth Amendment) Act, 1987.

(2) It shall come into force on such date as the Central Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette, appoint.

2. Amendment of the First Schedule.—In the First Schedule to the Constitution—
(a) under the heading 'I. THE STATES', Goa shall be inserted as a State;
(b) under the heading 'II. THE UNION TERRITORIES', Daman and Diu shall be specified as a Union Territory.

3. Amendment of the Fourth Schedule.—In the Fourth Schedule to the Constitution, the entry relating to Goa shall be inserted providing representation in the Council of States.

4. Insertion of new article 371I.—After article 371H of the Constitution, the following article shall be inserted, namely:—

'371I. Special provision with respect to the State of Goa.—Notwithstanding anything in this Constitution, the Legislative Assembly of the State of Goa shall consist of not less than thirty members.'

amendments.title: The Constitution (Fifty-seventh Amendment) Act, 1987
amendments.description: The Fifty-seventh Amendment amended Article 332 to ensure adequate reservation of seats for Scheduled Tribes in the Legislative Assemblies of the States of Arunachal Pradesh, Meghalaya, Mizoram and Nagaland. It empowered Parliament to determine by law the number of seats reserved for Scheduled Tribes in these States instead of applying the general principle of proportional reservation based strictly on population.

affectedArticles.change: Inserted clause (3A) to provide that, until Parliament otherwise provides by law, the reservation of seats for Scheduled Tribes in the Legislative Assemblies of Arunachal Pradesh, Meghalaya, Mizoram and Nagaland shall be determined in the manner specified, ensuring adequate representation.

amendments.fullText:
THE CONSTITUTION (FIFTY-SEVENTH AMENDMENT) ACT, 1987

[21st September, 1987.]

An Act further to amend the Constitution of India.

BE it enacted by Parliament in the Thirty-eighth Year of the Republic of India as follows:—

1. Short title.—This Act may be called the Constitution (Fifty-seventh Amendment) Act, 1987.

2. Amendment of article 332.—In article 332 of the Constitution, after clause (3), the following clause shall be inserted, namely:—

"(3A) Until the dissolution of the Legislative Assembly of the State of Arunachal Pradesh constituted under section 15 of the State of Arunachal Pradesh Act, 1986, or the dissolution of the Legislative Assembly of the State of Meghalaya or the State of Mizoram or the State of Nagaland, as the case may be, first constituted after the coming into force of the Constitution (Fifty-seventh Amendment) Act, 1987, the seats which shall be reserved for the Scheduled Tribes in the Legislative Assembly of any such State shall be such number as Parliament may by law determine."

amendments.title: The Constitution (Fifty-eighth Amendment) Act, 1987
amendments.description: The Fifty-eighth Amendment inserted Article 394A into the Constitution to provide for an authoritative text of the Constitution in the Hindi language. It empowered the President to publish, under his authority, the Hindi translation of the Constitution as amended from time to time and required every constitutional amendment enacted in English to be translated into Hindi. The Hindi text so published was declared to have the same authoritative status as the English text, subject to necessary adaptations for linguistic consistency.

newArticles.title: Authoritative text in the Hindi language
newArticles.change: Inserted new Article 394A providing for the publication and authoritative status of the Hindi text of the Constitution and of Constitution Amendment Acts.

amendments.fullText:
THE CONSTITUTION (FIFTY-EIGHTH AMENDMENT) ACT, 1987

[9th December, 1987.]

An Act further to amend the Constitution of India.

BE it enacted by Parliament in the Thirty-eighth Year of the Republic of India as follows:—

1. Short title.—This Act may be called the Constitution (Fifty-eighth Amendment) Act, 1987.

2. Insertion of new article 394A.—After article 394 of the Constitution, the following article shall be inserted, namely:—

"394A. Authoritative text in the Hindi language.—
(a) the President shall cause to be published under his authority the translation of this Constitution in the Hindi language, signed by the members of the Constituent Assembly, with such modifications as may be necessary to bring it in conformity with the language, style and terminology adopted in the authoritative texts of Central Acts in the Hindi language;

(b) the translation of every amendment of this Constitution made in the English language shall be published in the Hindi language under the authority of the President;

(c) the translation of this Constitution and of every amendment thereof published under clause (a) or clause (b) shall be construed to have the same meaning as the original text thereof in English, and if any difficulty arises in so construing any part of such translation, the President shall cause the same to be suitably revised;

(d) the translation of this Constitution and of every amendment thereof published under this article shall be deemed to be, for all purposes, its authoritative text in the Hindi language."

amendments.title: The Constitution (Fifty-ninth Amendment) Act, 1988
amendments.description: The Fifty-ninth Amendment empowered the President to declare a National Emergency in relation to the whole or any part of the State of Punjab on the ground of internal disturbance. It amended Article 352 for this special purpose, inserted Article 359A to suspend the enforcement of specified Fundamental Rights during such an emergency, and amended Article 356 to extend the maximum period of President's Rule in Punjab up to three years.

affectedArticles.change: Amended Article 352 to empower the President to proclaim an Emergency in relation to the whole or any part of the State of Punjab on the ground of internal disturbance.
Amended clause (5) to permit the continuance of a Proclamation of President's Rule in the State of Punjab for a period up to three years under specified conditions.

newArticles.title: Application of this Part during emergency to the State of Punjab
newArticles.change: Inserted Article 359A providing for suspension of the enforcement of specified Fundamental Rights during an Emergency relating to Punjab.

amendments.fullText:
THE CONSTITUTION (FIFTY-NINTH AMENDMENT) ACT, 1988

[30th March, 1988.]

An Act further to amend the Constitution of India.

BE it enacted by Parliament in the Thirty-ninth Year of the Republic of India as follows:—

1. Short title and commencement.—(1) This Act may be called the Constitution (Fifty-ninth Amendment) Act, 1988.

(2) It shall be deemed to have come into force on the 30th day of March, 1988.

2. Amendment of article 352.—Article 352 was amended to enable the President to issue a Proclamation of Emergency in relation to the whole or any part of the State of Punjab on the ground of internal disturbance.

3. Insertion of new article 359A.—After article 359, the following article was inserted, namely:—

"359A. Application of this Part during emergency to the State of Punjab.—Notwithstanding anything in this Constitution, where a Proclamation of Emergency is in operation in relation to the whole or any part of the State of Punjab, the provisions relating to enforcement of Fundamental Rights shall have effect subject to the modifications specified in this article."

4. Amendment of article 356.—Clause (5) of article 356 was amended to permit the continuance of a Proclamation issued under clause (1) in relation to the State of Punjab for a maximum period of three years, subject to the conditions specified therein.

amendments.title: The Constitution (Sixtieth Amendment) Act, 1988
amendments.description: The Sixtieth Amendment amended Article 276 to increase the maximum limit of taxes on professions, trades, callings and employments that may be imposed by States and local authorities. The ceiling was raised from Rs. 250 per annum to Rs. 2,500 per annum to account for inflation and the increased financial requirements of State Governments and local bodies.

affectedArticles.change: Amended clause (2) to increase the maximum amount of tax on professions, trades, callings and employments from two hundred and fifty rupees per annum to two thousand and five hundred rupees per annum.

amendments.fullText:
THE CONSTITUTION (SIXTIETH AMENDMENT) ACT, 1988

[20th December, 1988.]

An Act further to amend the Constitution of India.

BE it enacted by Parliament in the Thirty-ninth Year of the Republic of India as follows:—

1. Short title and commencement.—(1) This Act may be called the Constitution (Sixtieth Amendment) Act, 1988.

(2) It shall come into force at once.

2. Amendment of article 276.—In clause (2) of article 276 of the Constitution, for the words 'two hundred and fifty rupees per annum', the words 'two thousand and five hundred rupees per annum' shall be substituted.

amendments.title: The Constitution (Sixty-first Amendment) Act, 1988
amendments.description: The Sixty-first Amendment reduced the minimum voting age for elections to the House of the People and to the Legislative Assemblies of States from twenty-one years to eighteen years. It amended Article 326 with the objective of encouraging greater participation of the youth in the democratic process.

affectedArticles.change: Amended Article 326 by substituting the words 'eighteen years' for 'twenty-one years', thereby reducing the minimum voting age from 21 years to 18 years for elections to the House of the People and the Legislative Assemblies of States.

amendments.fullText:
THE CONSTITUTION (SIXTY-FIRST AMENDMENT) ACT, 1988

[28th March, 1989.]

An Act further to amend the Constitution of India.

BE it enacted by Parliament in the Fortieth Year of the Republic of India as follows:—

1. Short title and commencement.—(1) This Act may be called the Constitution (Sixty-first Amendment) Act, 1988.

(2) It shall come into force on such date as the Central Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette, appoint.

2. Amendment of article 326.—In article 326 of the Constitution, for the words 'twenty-one years', the words 'eighteen years' shall be substituted.

amendments.title: The Constitution (Sixty-second Amendment) Act, 1989
amendments.description: The Sixty-second Amendment extended for another ten years the reservation of seats for the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes in the House of the People and the Legislative Assemblies of the States, as well as the representation of the Anglo-Indian community by nomination in the House of the People and the Legislative Assemblies of the States. It amended Article 334 by extending these special provisions from forty years to fifty years from the commencement of the Constitution.

affectedArticles.change: Amended Article 334 by substituting the words 'fifty years' for 'forty years', thereby extending the reservation of seats for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes and the nomination of members of the Anglo-Indian community in the House of the People and the Legislative Assemblies of the States until 26 January 2000.

amendments.fullText:
THE CONSTITUTION (SIXTY-SECOND AMENDMENT) ACT, 1989

[20th December, 1989.]

An Act further to amend the Constitution of India.

BE it enacted by Parliament in the Fortieth Year of the Republic of India as follows:—

1. Short title and commencement.—(1) This Act may be called the Constitution (Sixty-second Amendment) Act, 1989.

(2) It shall come into force on the 25th day of January, 1990.

2. Amendment of article 334.—In article 334 of the Constitution, for the words 'forty years', the words 'fifty years' shall be substituted.

amendments.title: The Constitution (Sixty-third Amendment) Act, 1989
amendments.description: The Sixty-third Amendment repealed the special provisions introduced by the Fifty-ninth Amendment relating to the State of Punjab. It omitted Article 359A, which had provided for the suspension of the enforcement of specified Fundamental Rights during an Emergency in Punjab, and restored the normal constitutional provisions governing emergencies.

removedArticles.title: Application of this Part during emergency to the State of Punjab
removedArticles.change: Omitted Article 359A, thereby removing the special emergency provisions applicable to the State of Punjab that had been inserted by the Constitution (Fifty-ninth Amendment) Act, 1988.

amendments.fullText:
THE CONSTITUTION (SIXTY-THIRD AMENDMENT) ACT, 1989

[6th January, 1990.]

An Act further to amend the Constitution of India.

BE it enacted by Parliament in the Fortieth Year of the Republic of India as follows:—

1. Short title and commencement.—(1) This Act may be called the Constitution (Sixty-third Amendment) Act, 1989.

(2) It shall be deemed to have come into force on the 6th day of January, 1990.

2. Omission of article 359A.—Article 359A of the Constitution shall be omitted.

amendments.title: The Constitution (Sixty-fourth Amendment) Act, 1990
amendments.description: The Sixty-fourth Amendment amended Article 356 to extend the maximum period for which President's Rule could continue in the State of Punjab. It permitted the Proclamation issued under Article 356 in relation to Punjab to remain in force for up to three years and six months instead of the existing limit of three years, in view of the prevailing disturbed conditions in the State.

affectedArticles.change: Inserted a special proviso to clause (5) of Article 356 enabling the Proclamation of President's Rule in the State of Punjab to continue for a maximum period of three years and six months.

amendments.fullText:
THE CONSTITUTION (SIXTY-FOURTH AMENDMENT) ACT, 1990

[16th April, 1990.]

An Act further to amend the Constitution of India.

BE it enacted by Parliament in the Forty-first Year of the Republic of India as follows:—

1. Short title and commencement.—(1) This Act may be called the Constitution (Sixty-fourth Amendment) Act, 1990.

(2) It shall be deemed to have come into force on the 11th day of May, 1987.

2. Amendment of article 356.—In clause (5) of article 356 of the Constitution, after the second proviso, a further proviso was inserted to provide that in the case of the Proclamation issued under clause (1) on the 11th day of May, 1987, with respect to the State of Punjab, the reference to 'three years' shall be construed as a reference to 'three years and six months'.

amendments.title: The Constitution (Sixty-fifth Amendment) Act, 1990
amendments.description: The Sixty-fifth Amendment amended Article 338 to replace the office of the Special Officer for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes with a multi-member National Commission for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes. The amendment enlarged the Commission's functions by empowering it to investigate and monitor safeguards for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes, inquire into specific complaints, participate in the planning process for their socio-economic development, and submit reports to the President.

affectedArticles.change: Substituted Article 338 to provide for a multi-member National Commission for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes in place of the Special Officer for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes, and defined its composition, powers, duties and reporting functions.

amendments.fullText:
THE CONSTITUTION (SIXTY-FIFTH AMENDMENT) ACT, 1990

[12th March, 1992.]

An Act further to amend the Constitution of India.

BE it enacted by Parliament in the Forty-first Year of the Republic of India as follows:—

1. Short title and commencement.—(1) This Act may be called the Constitution (Sixty-fifth Amendment) Act, 1990.

(2) It shall come into force on such date as the Central Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette, appoint.

2. Substitution of article 338.—For article 338 of the Constitution, the following article shall be substituted, namely:—

"338. National Commission for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.—The amendment substituted the existing Article 338 to establish a National Commission for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes consisting of a Chairperson, Vice-Chairperson and other Members. It empowered the Commission to investigate and monitor constitutional safeguards, inquire into complaints regarding deprivation of rights, participate in planning for socio-economic development, present annual and special reports to the President, and perform such other functions as may be specified by the President subject to law made by Parliament."

amendments.title: The Constitution (Sixty-sixth Amendment) Act, 1990
amendments.description: The Sixty-sixth Amendment inserted fifty-five State Acts relating to land reforms into the Ninth Schedule to protect them from being challenged in courts on the ground that they were inconsistent with or took away or abridged any of the Fundamental Rights conferred by Part III of the Constitution. These enactments primarily dealt with agrarian reforms, ceiling on land holdings, tenancy reforms and related matters.

affectedSchedules.change: Amended the Ninth Schedule by inserting fifty-five State Acts relating to land reforms and agrarian legislation to provide them constitutional protection against challenge on the ground of violation of Fundamental Rights.

amendments.fullText:
THE CONSTITUTION (SIXTY-SIXTH AMENDMENT) ACT, 1990

[7th June, 1990.]

An Act further to amend the Constitution of India.

BE it enacted by Parliament in the Forty-first Year of the Republic of India as follows:—

1. Short title.—This Act may be called the Constitution (Sixty-sixth Amendment) Act, 1990.

2. Amendment of the Ninth Schedule.—In the Ninth Schedule to the Constitution, after Entry 257, Entries 258 to 312 (comprising fifty-five State Acts relating to land reforms and agrarian legislation) shall be inserted.

amendments.title: The Constitution (Sixty-seventh Amendment) Act, 1990
amendments.description: The Sixty-seventh Amendment further amended Article 356 to extend the maximum period for which the Proclamation of President's Rule in the State of Punjab could remain in force. It increased the permissible period from three years and six months to four years in view of the continuing disturbed conditions in the State.

affectedArticles.change: Amended clause (5) of Article 356 by further modifying the special proviso relating to the Proclamation issued in respect of the State of Punjab on 11 May 1987, extending the maximum permissible duration of President's Rule from three years and six months to four years.

amendments.fullText:
THE CONSTITUTION (SIXTY-SEVENTH AMENDMENT) ACT, 1990

[4th October, 1990.]

An Act further to amend the Constitution of India.

BE it enacted by Parliament in the Forty-first Year of the Republic of India as follows:—

1. Short title and commencement.—(1) This Act may be called the Constitution (Sixty-seventh Amendment) Act, 1990.

(2) It shall be deemed to have come into force on the 4th day of October, 1990.

2. Amendment of article 356.—In clause (5) of article 356 of the Constitution, in the special proviso relating to the Proclamation issued under clause (1) on the 11th day of May, 1987, in relation to the State of Punjab, for the words 'three years and six months', the words 'four years' shall be substituted.

amendments.title: The Constitution (Sixty-eighth Amendment) Act, 1991
amendments.description: The Sixty-eighth Amendment further amended Article 356 to extend the maximum period for which the Proclamation of President's Rule in the State of Punjab could remain in force. It increased the permissible period from four years to five years in view of the continuing disturbed conditions prevailing in the State.

affectedArticles.change: Amended clause (5) of Article 356 by further modifying the special proviso relating to the Proclamation issued in respect of the State of Punjab on 11 May 1987, extending the maximum permissible duration of President's Rule from four years to five years.

amendments.fullText:
THE CONSTITUTION (SIXTY-EIGHTH AMENDMENT) ACT, 1991

[12th March, 1991.]

An Act further to amend the Constitution of India.

BE it enacted by Parliament in the Forty-second Year of the Republic of India as follows:—

1. Short title and commencement.—(1) This Act may be called the Constitution (Sixty-eighth Amendment) Act, 1991.

(2) It shall be deemed to have come into force on the 12th day of March, 1991.

2. Amendment of article 356.—In clause (5) of article 356 of the Constitution, in the special proviso relating to the Proclamation issued under clause (1) on the 11th day of May, 1987, in relation to the State of Punjab, for the words 'four years', the words 'five years' shall be substituted.

amendments.title: The Constitution (Sixty-ninth Amendment) Act, 1991
amendments.description: The Sixty-ninth Amendment conferred a special constitutional status on the Union Territory of Delhi by redesignating it as the National Capital Territory of Delhi. It inserted Articles 239AA and 239AB to provide for a Legislative Assembly, a Council of Ministers headed by a Chief Minister, and special provisions regarding the administration of the National Capital Territory, while reserving matters relating to public order, police and land to the Union. The Amendment also changed the designation of the Administrator to Lieutenant Governor.

newArticles.title: Special provisions with respect to Delhi
newArticles.change: Inserted Article 239AA providing for the National Capital Territory of Delhi, a Legislative Assembly, a Council of Ministers headed by the Chief Minister, distribution of legislative powers, and the designation of the Administrator as the Lieutenant Governor.

newArticles.title: Provision in case of failure of constitutional machinery
newArticles.change: Inserted Article 239AB empowering the President to suspend the operation of Article 239AA or any law made thereunder where the administration of the National Capital Territory cannot be carried on in accordance with Article 239AA.

amendments.fullText:
THE CONSTITUTION (SIXTY-NINTH AMENDMENT) ACT, 1991

[1st February, 1992.]

An Act further to amend the Constitution of India.

BE it enacted by Parliament in the Forty-second Year of the Republic of India as follows:—

1. Short title and commencement.—(1) This Act may be called the Constitution (Sixty-ninth Amendment) Act, 1991.

(2) It shall come into force on such date as the Central Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette, appoint.

2. Insertion of new articles 239AA and 239AB.—After article 239A of the Constitution, the following articles shall be inserted, namely:—

"239AA. Special provisions with respect to Delhi.—The Union Territory of Delhi shall be called the National Capital Territory of Delhi and the administrator thereof appointed under article 239 shall be designated as the Lieutenant Governor. There shall be a Legislative Assembly for the National Capital Territory and a Council of Ministers with the Chief Minister at the head to aid and advise the Lieutenant Governor, subject to the provisions of this article. The Legislative Assembly shall have power to make laws with respect to matters in the State List and Concurrent List except public order, police and land.

239AB. Provision in case of failure of constitutional machinery.—If the President, on receipt of a report from the Lieutenant Governor or otherwise, is satisfied that the administration of the National Capital Territory cannot be carried on in accordance with Article 239AA or any law made thereunder, he may by order suspend the operation of any provision of Article 239AA or of such law and make such incidental and consequential provisions as appear necessary for administering the National Capital Territory."

amendments.title: The Constitution (Seventieth Amendment) Act, 1992
amendments.description: The Seventieth Amendment amended Article 54 to include the elected members of the Legislative Assemblies of the National Capital Territory of Delhi and the Union Territory of Pondicherry (now Puducherry) in the electoral college for the election of the President of India. Prior to this amendment, only the elected members of the Legislative Assemblies of the States were included in the electoral college.

affectedArticles.change: Amended Article 54 to include the elected members of the Legislative Assemblies of the National Capital Territory of Delhi and the Union Territory of Pondicherry in the electoral college for the election of the President of India.

amendments.fullText:
THE CONSTITUTION (SEVENTIETH AMENDMENT) ACT, 1992

[21st December, 1991.]

An Act further to amend the Constitution of India.

BE it enacted by Parliament in the Forty-second Year of the Republic of India as follows:—

1. Short title and commencement.—(1) This Act may be called the Constitution (Seventieth Amendment) Act, 1992.

(2) It shall come into force on such date as the Central Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette, appoint.

2. Amendment of article 54.—In article 54 of the Constitution, after the words 'Legislative Assemblies of the States', the words 'and of the elected members of the Legislative Assemblies of the Union territories of Delhi and Pondicherry' shall be inserted.

amendments.title: The Constitution (Seventy-first Amendment) Act, 1992
amendments.description: The Seventy-first Amendment amended the Eighth Schedule to the Constitution by including three more languages—Konkani, Manipuri and Nepali. With this amendment, the total number of languages recognized in the Eighth Schedule increased from fifteen to eighteen.

affectedSchedules.change: Amended the Eighth Schedule by including Konkani, Manipuri and Nepali as recognized languages of the Constitution.

amendments.fullText:
THE CONSTITUTION (SEVENTY-FIRST AMENDMENT) ACT, 1992

[31st August, 1992.]

An Act further to amend the Constitution of India.

BE it enacted by Parliament in the Forty-third Year of the Republic of India as follows:—

1. Short title.—This Act may be called the Constitution (Seventy-first Amendment) Act, 1992.

2. Amendment of the Eighth Schedule.—In the Eighth Schedule to the Constitution, after the entries 'Kashmiri', 'Malayalam' and 'Marathi', the entries 'Konkani', 'Manipuri' and 'Nepali' shall respectively be inserted.

amendments.title: The Constitution (Seventy-second Amendment) Act, 1992
amendments.description: The Seventy-second Amendment amended Article 332 to provide for reservation of seats for the Scheduled Tribes in the Legislative Assembly of the State of Tripura. The amendment ensured adequate representation of Scheduled Tribes following the reorganization of constituencies in the State.

affectedArticles.change: Inserted clause (3B) to provide for reservation of seats for Scheduled Tribes in the Legislative Assembly of the State of Tripura until the readjustment of constituencies after the first census conducted after the year 2000.

amendments.fullText:
THE CONSTITUTION (SEVENTY-SECOND AMENDMENT) ACT, 1992

[5th April, 1992.]

An Act further to amend the Constitution of India.

BE it enacted by Parliament in the Forty-third Year of the Republic of India as follows:—

1. Short title and commencement.—(1) This Act may be called the Constitution (Seventy-second Amendment) Act, 1992.

(2) It shall come into force on such date as the Central Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette, appoint.

2. Amendment of article 332.—In article 332 of the Constitution, after clause (3A), the following clause shall be inserted, namely:—

"(3B) Notwithstanding anything contained in clause (3), until the readjustment under article 170 takes effect on the basis of the first census after the year 2000 has been published, the number of seats reserved for the Scheduled Tribes in the Legislative Assembly of the State of Tripura shall be such as Parliament may by law determine."

amendments.title: The Constitution (Seventy-third Amendment) Act, 1992
amendments.description: The Seventy-third Amendment granted constitutional status to Panchayati Raj Institutions (PRIs) by adding Part IX (Articles 243 to 243-O) and the Eleventh Schedule to the Constitution. It established a three-tier system of Panchayati Raj, mandated regular elections every five years, provided for reservation of seats for Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes and women, and established State Election Commissions and State Finance Commissions. The amendment gave effect to Article 40 of the Directive Principles of State Policy, which directs the State to organise village panchayats as units of self-government.

affectedArticles.change: Gave effect to Article 40 of the Directive Principles of State Policy, which directs the State to take steps to organise village panchayats and endow them with such powers and authority as may be necessary to enable them to function as units of self-government.

newArticles.change: Inserted to define the basic structure and composition of Panchayats, including the establishment of Gram Sabha, three-tier system, direct elections, and reservation of seats for SCs, STs and women.
Inserted to define the Gram Sabha as a body consisting of persons registered in the electoral rolls relating to a village comprised within the area of Panchayat at the village level.
Inserted to provide for the constitution of Panchayats at the village, intermediate and district levels in every State.
Inserted to provide for the composition of Panchayats, including the manner of election of members and Chairpersons.

Inserted to provide for reservation of seats for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes in every Panchayat in proportion to their population, and reservation of not less than one-third of the total number of seats for women (including women from SC/ST categories).
Inserted to fix the duration of Panchayats at five years and provide for elections within six months in case of dissolution.
Inserted to prescribe disqualifications for membership of Panchayats and the procedure for deciding such questions.

Inserted to empower State Legislatures to devolve powers and responsibilities upon Panchayats with respect to the preparation of plans for economic development and social justice, and for the implementation of development schemes as may be entrusted to them.
Inserted to empower State Legislatures to authorise Panchayats to levy, collect and appropriate taxes, duties, tolls and fees.

Inserted to provide for the constitution of a Finance Commission every five years to review the financial position of Panchayats and make recommendations on the distribution of taxes, duties, tolls and fees between the State and Panchayats.
Inserted to provide for the audit of accounts of Panchayats.
Inserted to provide for the superintendence, direction and control of elections to Panchayats to be vested in a State Election Commission.
Inserted to provide for the application of the provisions of Part IX to Union territories.
Inserted to exclude certain areas and States (such as Nagaland, Meghalaya, Mizoram and certain Scheduled Areas) from the application of Part IX, subject to certain conditions.
Inserted to provide for the continuance of existing laws and Panchayats until amended or repealed.
Inserted to bar the jurisdiction of courts in matters relating to elections to Panchayats.

newParts.title: PART IX – THE PANCHAYATS
newParts.change: Inserted after Part VIII of the Constitution, containing Articles 243 to 243-O, providing for the establishment, composition, powers, functions and finances of Panchayati Raj Institutions across India.

affectedSchedules.change: Inserted the Eleventh Schedule containing 29 subjects (entries 1 to 29) which may be devolved to Panchayats by State Legislatures, including Agriculture, Land Improvement, Minor Irrigation, Animal Husbandry, Fisheries, Social Forestry, Minor Forest Produce, Small Scale Industries, Rural Housing, Drinking Water, Fuel and Fodder, Roads, Education, Health and Sanitation, Women and Child Development, Social Welfare, Public Distribution System, Maintenance of Community Assets, etc.

amendments.fullText:
THE CONSTITUTION (SEVENTY-THIRD AMENDMENT) ACT, 1992

[20th April, 1993.]

An Act further to amend the Constitution of India.

BE it enacted by Parliament in the Forty-third Year of the Republic of India as follows:—

1. Short title and commencement.—(1) This Act may be called the Constitution (Seventy-third Amendment) Act, 1992. (2) It shall come into force on such date as the Central Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette, appoint.

2. Insertion of new Part IX.—After Part VIII of the Constitution, the following Part shall be inserted, namely:—

'PART IX
THE PANCHAYATS

243. Definitions.—In this Part, unless the context otherwise requires,—
(a) "district" means a district in a State;
(b) "Gram Sabha" means a body consisting of persons registered in the electoral rolls relating to a village comprised within the area of Panchayat at the village level;
(c) "intermediate level" means a level between the village and district levels specified by the Governor of a State by public notification to be the intermediate level for the purposes of this Part;
(d) "Panchayat" means an institution (by whatever name called) of self-government constituted under article 243B, for the rural areas;
(e) "Panchayat area" means the territorial area of a Panchayat;
(f) "population" means the population as ascertained at the last preceding census of which the relevant figures have been published;
(g) "village" means a village specified by the Governor by public notification to be a village for the purposes of this Part and includes a group of villages so specified.

243A. Gram Sabha.—A Gram Sabha may exercise such powers and perform such functions at the village level as the Legislature of a State may, by law, provide.

243B. Constitution of Panchayats.—(1) There shall be constituted in every State, Panchayats at the village, intermediate and district levels in accordance with the provisions of this Part.
(2) Notwithstanding anything in clause (1), Panchayats at the intermediate level may not be constituted in a State having a population not exceeding twenty lakhs.

243C. Composition of Panchayats.—(1) Subject to the provisions of this Part, the Legislature of a State may, by law, make provisions with respect to the composition of Panchayats.
(2) The ratio between the population of the territorial area of a Panchayat at any level and the number of seats in such Panchayat to be filled by election shall, so far as practicable, be the same throughout the State.
(3) All the seats in a Panchayat shall be filled by persons chosen by direct election from territorial constituencies in the Panchayat area.
(4) The Chairperson of a Panchayat at the village level shall be elected in such manner as the Legislature of a State may, by law, provide.

243D. Reservation of seats.—(1) Seats shall be reserved for—
(a) the Scheduled Castes; and
(b) the Scheduled Tribes,
in every Panchayat and the number of seats so reserved shall bear, as nearly as may be, the same proportion to the total number of seats to be filled by direct election in that Panchayat as the population of the Scheduled Castes in that Panchayat area or of the Scheduled Tribes in that Panchayat area bears to the total population of that area and such seats may be allotted by rotation to different constituencies in a Panchayat.
(2) Not less than one-third of the total number of seats reserved under clause (1) shall be reserved for women belonging to the Scheduled Castes or, as the case may be, the Scheduled Tribes.
(3) Not less than one-third (including the number of seats reserved for women belonging to the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes) of the total number of seats to be filled by direct election in every Panchayat shall be reserved for women and such seats may be allotted by rotation to different constituencies in a Panchayat.
(4) The offices of the Chairpersons in the Panchayats at the village or any other level shall be reserved for the Scheduled Castes, the Scheduled Tribes and women in such manner as the Legislature of a State may, by law, provide.

243E. Duration of Panchayats, etc.—(1) Every Panchayat, unless sooner dissolved under any law for the time being in force, shall continue for five years from the date appointed for its first meeting and no longer.
(2) No amendment of any law for the time being in force shall have the effect of causing dissolution of a Panchayat at any level, which is functioning immediately before such amendment, till the expiration of its duration specified in clause (1).
(3) An election to constitute a Panchayat shall be completed—
(a) before the expiry of its duration specified in clause (1);
(b) before the expiration of a period of six months from the date of its dissolution:
Provided that where the remainder of the period for which the dissolved Panchayat would have continued is less than six months, it shall not be necessary to hold any election under this clause for constituting the Panchayat for such period.

243F. Disqualifications for membership.—(1) A person shall be disqualified for being chosen as, and for being, a member of a Panchayat—
(a) if he is so disqualified by or under any law for the time being in force for the purposes of elections to the Legislature of the State concerned;
(b) if he is so disqualified by or under any law made by the Legislature of the State.
(2) If any question arises as to whether a member of a Panchayat has become subject to any of the disqualifications mentioned in clause (1), the question shall be referred for the decision of such authority and in such manner as the Legislature of a State may, by law, provide.

243G. Powers, authority and responsibilities of Panchayats.—Subject to the provisions of this Constitution, the Legislature of a State may, by law, endow the Panchayats with such powers and authority as may be necessary to enable them to function as institutions of self-government and such law may contain provisions for the devolution of powers and responsibilities upon Panchayats at the appropriate level, subject to such conditions as may be specified therein, with respect to—
(a) the preparation of plans for economic development and social justice;
(b) the implementation of schemes for economic development and social justice as may be entrusted to them including those in relation to the matters listed in the Eleventh Schedule.

243H. Powers to impose taxes by, and Funds of, the Panchayats.—The Legislature of a State may, by law,—
(a) authorise a Panchayat to levy, collect and appropriate such taxes, duties, tolls and fees in accordance with such procedure and subject to such limits;
(b) assign to a Panchayat such taxes, duties, tolls and fees levied and collected by the State Government for such purposes and subject to such conditions and limits;
(c) provide for making such grants-in-aid to the Panchayats from the Consolidated Fund of the State; and
(d) provide for constitution of such funds for crediting all moneys received by or on behalf of the Panchayats and also the withdrawal of such moneys therefrom, as may be specified in the law.

243I. Constitution of Finance Commission to review financial position.—(1) The Governor of a State shall, as soon as may be within one year from the commencement of the Constitution (Seventy-third Amendment) Act, 1992, and thereafter at the expiration of every fifth year, constitute a Finance Commission to review the financial position of the Panchayats and to make recommendations to the Governor as to—
(a) the principles which should govern—
(i) the distribution between the State and the Panchayats of the net proceeds of the taxes, duties, tolls and fees leviable by the State, which may be divided between them under this Part and the allocation between the Panchayats at all levels of their respective shares of such proceeds;
(ii) the determination of the taxes, duties, tolls and fees which may be assigned to, or appropriated by, the Panchayats;
(iii) the grants-in-aid to the Panchayats from the Consolidated Fund of the State;
(b) the measures needed to improve the financial position of the Panchayats;
(c) any other matter referred to the Finance Commission by the Governor in the interests of sound finance of the Panchayats.
(2) The Legislature of a State may, by law, provide for the composition of the Commission, the qualifications of its members and the manner in which they shall be selected.
(3) The Commission shall determine its procedure and shall have such powers in the performance of its functions as the Legislature of the State may, by law, confer on it.
(4) The Governor shall cause every recommendation made by the Commission under this article together with an explanatory memorandum as to the action taken thereon to be laid before the Legislature of the State.

243J. Audit of accounts of Panchayats.—The Legislature of a State may, by law, make provisions with respect to the maintenance of accounts by the Panchayats and the auditing of such accounts.

243K. Elections to the Panchayats.—(1) The superintendence, direction and control of the preparation of electoral rolls for, and the conduct of, all elections to the Panchayats shall be vested in a State Election Commission consisting of a State Election Commissioner to be appointed by the Governor.
(2) Subject to the provisions of any law made by the Legislature of a State, the conditions of service and tenure of office of the State Election Commissioner shall be such as the Governor may by rule determine.
(3) The State Election Commissioner shall not be removed from his office except in like manner and on the like grounds as a Judge of a High Court and the conditions of service of the State Election Commissioner shall not be varied to his disadvantage after his appointment.
(4) The Governor of a State shall, when so requested by the State Election Commission, make available to the State Election Commission such staff as may be necessary for the discharge of the functions conferred on the State Election Commission by clause (1).

243L. Application to Union territories.—The provisions of this Part shall apply to the Union territories and shall, in their application to a Union territory, have effect as if the references to the Governor of a State were references to the Administrator of the Union territory appointed under article 239 and references to the Legislature or the Legislative Assembly of a State were references, in relation to a Union territory having a Legislative Assembly, to that Legislative Assembly.

243M. Part not to apply to certain areas.—(1) Nothing in this Part shall apply to the Scheduled Areas referred to in clause (1), and the tribal areas referred to in clause (2), of article 244.
(2) Nothing in this Part shall apply to—
(a) the States of Nagaland, Meghalaya and Mizoram;
(b) the hill areas in the State of Manipur for which District Councils exist under any law for the time being in force.
(3) Nothing in this Part shall be construed to affect the functions and powers of the District Councils in the States of Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram.

243N. Continuance of existing laws and Panchayats.—Notwithstanding anything in this Part, any provision of any law relating to Panchayats in force in a State immediately before the commencement of the Constitution (Seventy-third Amendment) Act, 1992, which is inconsistent with the provisions of this Part, shall continue to be in force until amended or repealed by a competent Legislature or other competent authority or until the expiration of one year from such commencement, whichever is earlier:
Provided that all the Panchayats existing immediately before such commencement shall continue till the expiration of their duration unless sooner dissolved by a resolution passed to that effect by the Legislative Assembly of that State or, in the case of a State having a Legislative Council, by both Houses of the Legislature of that State.

243O. Bar to interference by courts in electoral matters.—Notwithstanding anything in this Constitution,—
(a) the validity of any law relating to the delimitation of constituencies or the allotment of seats to such constituencies, made or purporting to be made under article 243K, shall not be called in question in any court;
(b) no election to any Panchayat shall be called in question except by an election petition presented to such authority and in such manner as may be provided for by or under any law made by the Legislature of a State.'

3. Insertion of Eleventh Schedule.—After the Tenth Schedule to the Constitution, the following Schedule shall be inserted, namely:—

'ELEVENTH SCHEDULE
[Article 243G]

1. Agriculture, including agricultural extension.
2. Land improvement, implementation of land reforms, land consolidation and soil conservation.
3. Minor irrigation, water management and watershed development.
4. Animal husbandry, dairying and poultry.
5. Fisheries.
6. Social forestry and farm forestry.
7. Minor forest produce.
8. Small scale industries, including food processing industries.
9. Khadi, village and cottage industries.
10. Rural housing.
11. Drinking water.
12. Fuel and fodder.
13. Roads, culverts, bridges, ferries, waterways and other means of communication.
14. Rural electrification, including distribution of electricity.
15. Non-conventional energy sources.
16. Poverty alleviation programme.
17. Education, including primary and secondary schools.
18. Technical training and vocational education.
19. Adult and non-formal education.
20. Libraries.
21. Cultural activities.
22. Markets and fairs.
23. Health and sanitation, including hospitals, primary health centres and dispensaries.
24. Family welfare.
25. Women and child development.
26. Social welfare, including welfare of the handicapped and mentally retarded.
27. Welfare of the weaker sections, and in particular, of the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes.
28. Public distribution system.
29. Maintenance of community assets.

4. Amendment of article 40.—In article 40 of the Constitution, for the words 'shall take steps to organise village panchayats', the words 'shall take steps to organise village panchayats and endow them with such powers and authority as may be necessary to enable them to function as units of self-government' shall be substituted.

5. Amendment of article 246.—In article 246 of the Constitution, in clause (3), for the words 'subject to clauses (1) and (2)', the words 'subject to clauses (1) and (2) and to the provisions of Part IX' shall be substituted.

amendments.title: The Constitution (Seventy-fourth Amendment) Act, 1992
amendments.description: The Seventy-fourth Amendment granted constitutional status to urban local bodies by adding Part IXA (Articles 243P to 243ZG) and the Twelfth Schedule to the Constitution. It mandated the constitution of three types of municipalities—Nagar Panchayats for transitional areas, Municipal Councils for smaller urban areas, and Municipal Corporations for larger urban areas. The amendment provided for regular elections every five years, reservation of seats for Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes and women, constitution of Ward Committees, District Planning Committees and Metropolitan Planning Committees, and established State Election Commissions and State Finance Commissions for municipalities. It also provided for the devolution of powers and responsibilities upon municipalities with respect to the preparation of plans for economic development and social justice, and for the implementation of development schemes as enumerated in the Twelfth Schedule.

newArticles.change: Inserted to define the key terms used in Part IXA, including 'Committee', 'district', 'Metropolitan area', 'Municipal area', 'Municipality', 'Panchayat', and 'population'.

Inserted to mandate the constitution of three types of municipalities in every State—(a) Nagar Panchayat for transitional areas, (b) Municipal Council for smaller urban areas, and (c) Municipal Corporation for larger urban areas. Also provides for the specification of industrial townships.

Inserted to provide for the composition of municipalities, including direct election of members from territorial constituencies (wards), and the representation of persons having special knowledge or experience in municipal administration, MPs, MLAs, MLCs, and Chairpersons of Committees (with nominated members having no voting rights).

Inserted to provide for the constitution of Ward Committees in municipalities with a population of three lakhs or more, consisting of one or more wards, and to enable the State Legislature to make provisions for their composition and functions.

Inserted to provide for reservation of seats for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes in every municipality in proportion to their population, and reservation of not less than one-third of the total number of seats for women (including women from SC/ST categories). Also provides for reservation of the offices of Chairpersons for SCs, STs and women.
Inserted to fix the duration of municipalities at five years and provide for elections within six months in case of dissolution.
Inserted to prescribe disqualifications for membership of municipalities and the procedure for deciding such questions.

Inserted to empower State Legislatures to devolve powers and responsibilities upon municipalities with respect to the preparation of plans for economic development and social justice, and for the implementation of development schemes as may be entrusted to them, including those in relation to the matters listed in the Twelfth Schedule.

Inserted to empower State Legislatures to authorise municipalities to levy, collect and appropriate taxes, duties, tolls and fees, assign such taxes to municipalities, provide for grants-in-aid, and constitute funds for municipalities.

Inserted to provide for the constitution of a Finance Commission every five years to review the financial position of municipalities and make recommendations on the distribution of taxes, duties, tolls and fees between the State and municipalities, and on grants-in-aid.
Inserted to provide for the audit of accounts of municipalities.
Inserted to provide for the superintendence, direction and control of elections to municipalities to be vested in a State Election Commission.
Inserted to provide for the application of the provisions of Part IXA to Union territories.

Inserted to exclude certain areas (such as Scheduled Areas and tribal areas referred to in Article 244) from the application of Part IXA, and to provide that nothing in Part IXA shall affect the functions and powers of the District Councils in the States of Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram.

Inserted to provide for the constitution of District Planning Committees in every district to consolidate the plans prepared by Panchayats and municipalities and to prepare a draft development plan for the district as a whole.
Inserted to provide for the constitution of Metropolitan Planning Committees in every metropolitan area to prepare a draft development plan for the metropolitan area as a whole.
Inserted to provide for the continuance of existing laws and municipalities until amended or repealed.
Inserted to bar the jurisdiction of courts in matters relating to elections to municipalities.

newParts.title: PART IXA – THE MUNICIPALITIES
newParts.change: Inserted after Part IX of the Constitution, containing Articles 243P to 243ZG, providing for the establishment, composition, powers, functions and finances of urban local bodies (municipalities) across India.

affectedSchedules.change: Inserted the Twelfth Schedule containing 18 subjects (entries 1 to 18) which may be devolved to municipalities by State Legislatures, including Urban Planning, Regulation of land-use, Roads and bridges, Water supply, Public health and sanitation, Fire services, Urban forestry, Safeguarding the interests of weaker sections, Slum improvement, Urban poverty alleviation, Provision of urban amenities, Promotion of cultural, educational and aesthetic aspects, Burials and burial grounds, Cattle pounds, Vital statistics, Regulation of slaughter houses, and maintenance of cremation grounds.

amendments.fullText:
THE CONSTITUTION (SEVENTY-FOURTH AMENDMENT) ACT, 1992

[20th April, 1993.]

An Act further to amend the Constitution of India.

BE it enacted by Parliament in the Forty-third Year of the Republic of India as follows:—

1. Short title and commencement.—(1) This Act may be called the Constitution (Seventy-fourth Amendment) Act, 1992. (2) It shall come into force on such date as the Central Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette, appoint.

2. Insertion of new Part IXA.—After Part IX of the Constitution, the following Part shall be inserted, namely:—

'PART IXA
THE MUNICIPALITIES

243P. Definitions.—In this Part, unless the context otherwise requires,—
(a) "Committee" means a Committee constituted under article 243S;
(b) "district" means a district of a State;
